title.zh: 卷二百二十列傳第一百四十五 東夷
title.raw: 卷二百二十列傳第一百四十五 東夷 Volume 220 Biographies 145: Eastern Barbarians

sentences.zh: 高麗 百濟 新羅 倭、日本

translations.literal: Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, Wa, Japan
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, and Wa (Japan)

sentences.zh: 高麗，本扶餘別種也。

translations.literal: Goguryeo was originally a separate branch of the Fuyu people.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo was originally a distinct offshoot of the Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 地東跨海距新羅，南亦跨海距百濟，西北度遼水與營州接，北靺鞨。

translations.literal: Its territory eastward crosses the sea to border Silla; southward it also crosses the sea to border Baekje; northwest it crosses the Liao River and adjoins Ying Prefecture; northward it borders the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: To the east its land reaches across the sea to Silla; to the south it likewise crosses the sea to Baekje; to the northwest it crosses the Liao River and meets Ying Prefecture; to the north lies Mohe country.

sentences.zh: 其君居平壤城，亦謂長安城，漢樂浪郡也，去京師五千里而贏，隨山屈繚爲郛，南涯浿水，王築宮其左。

translations.literal: The ruler dwells at Pyongyang, also called Chang'an City—the Han commandery of Lelang—more than five thousand li from the capital in excess, with the outer wall winding along the hills; the southern margin is the Pae River, and the king built his palace to its left.
translations.idiomatic: The king resides at Pyongyang, also known as Chang'an City, on the site of the Han commandery of Lelang—over five thousand li from the capital. The city wall follows the bending hills; the Pae River marks the southern edge, and the royal palace stands on its east bank.

sentences.zh: 又有國內城、漢城，號別都。

translations.literal: There are also the Inner Capital and Han City, called secondary capitals.
translations.idiomatic: There are also the Inner Capital and Han City, styled as secondary capitals.

sentences.zh: 水有大遼、少遼：大遼出靺鞨西南山，南曆安市城；

translations.literal: Waters include the Greater Liao and Lesser Liao: the Greater Liao issues from the southwestern mountains of the Mohe and flows south past An City;
translations.idiomatic: The rivers include the Greater Liao and Lesser Liao: the Greater Liao rises in the southwestern mountains of Mohe country and runs south past An City;

sentences.zh: 少遼出遼山西，亦南流，有梁水出塞外，西行與之合。

translations.literal: the Lesser Liao issues from west of the Liao mountains and also flows south; there is the Liang River that issues beyond the frontier and flows west to join it.
translations.idiomatic: the Lesser Liao rises west of the Liao range and likewise flows south; the Liang River comes from beyond the passes and runs west to meet it.

sentences.zh: 有馬訾水出靺鞨之白山，色若鴨頭，號鴨淥水，曆國內城西，與鹽難水合，又西南至安市，入於海。

translations.literal: There is the Maze River that issues from White Mountain in Mohe country, colored like a duck's head, called the Yalu River; it passes west of the Inner Capital, joins the Yannan River, then turns southwest to An City and enters the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Maze River rises on White Mountain in Mohe territory; its hue is like a drake's head, whence it is called the Yalu. It runs west of the Inner Capital, joins the Yannan River, then turns southwest to An City and empties into the sea.

sentences.zh: 而平壤在鴨淥東南，以巨艫濟人，因恃以爲塹。

translations.literal: Pyongyang lies southeast of the Yalu; they ferry people in great ships and rely on it as a moat.
translations.idiomatic: Pyongyang lies southeast of the Yalu; they cross in large vessels and treat the river as their defensive moat.

sentences.zh: 官凡十二級：曰大對廬，或曰吐捽；

translations.literal: Officials number twelve ranks: called Grand Tae-du-ru, or also Tu-sol;
translations.idiomatic: There are twelve official ranks: the first is Grand Tae-du-ru, also called Tu-sol;

sentences.zh: 曰鬱折，主圖簿者；

translations.literal: called Yu-che, who oversees registers;
translations.idiomatic: Yu-che, who keeps the registers;

sentences.zh: 曰太大使者；

translations.literal: called Grand Envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Envoy;

sentences.zh: 曰帛衣頭大兄，所謂帛衣者，先人也，秉國政，三歲一易，善職則否，凡代日，有不服則相攻，王爲閉宮守，勝者聽爲之；

translations.literal: called Head Elder Brother in White Robes—so-called white robes are elders—who hold state power, changed every three years unless they perform well, then not; on each change day, if there is dissent they attack one another, the king shuts the palace and holds it, and the victor is allowed to take office;
translations.idiomatic: Head Elder Brother in White Robes—the 'white robes' are the elders who wield state power, rotated every three years unless a man serves well enough to remain. On each rotation day, rivals who refuse to yield fight one another while the king barricades the palace; the victor is then allowed to govern.

sentences.zh: 曰大使者；

translations.literal: called Envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Envoy;

sentences.zh: 曰大兄；

translations.literal: called Elder Brother;
translations.idiomatic: Elder Brother;

sentences.zh: 曰上位使者；

translations.literal: called Superior Envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Superior Envoy;

sentences.zh: 曰諸兄；

translations.literal: called Various Brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Various Brothers;

sentences.zh: 曰小使者；

translations.literal: called Junior Envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Junior Envoy;

sentences.zh: 曰過節；

translations.literal: called Guo-jie;
translations.idiomatic: Guo-jie;

sentences.zh: 曰先人；

translations.literal: called Elder;
translations.idiomatic: Elder;

sentences.zh: 曰古鄒大加。

translations.literal: called Gu-gu Grand Ga.
translations.idiomatic: and Gu-gu Grand Ga.

sentences.zh: 其州縣六十。

translations.literal: Its prefectures and counties number sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The realm comprises sixty prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 大城置傉薩一，比都督；

translations.literal: Each great city has one Lu-sa, comparable to a military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Each major city has a Lu-sa, equivalent to a Tang military commissioner;

sentences.zh: 餘城置處閭近支，亦號道使，比刺史。

translations.literal: other cities have Chu-lyu and Jin-zhi, also called circuit envoys, comparable to prefects.
translations.idiomatic: lesser cities have Chu-lyu and Jin-zhi officers, also styled circuit envoys, equivalent to prefects.

sentences.zh: 有參佐，分幹。

translations.literal: There are aides who divide duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each has aides who divide administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 有大模達，比衛將軍；

translations.literal: there is the Grand Mo-da, comparable to a Guard General;
translations.idiomatic: There is the Grand Mo-da, equivalent to a Guard General;

sentences.zh: 末客，比中郎將。

translations.literal: and Mo-ke, comparable to a General of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: and the Mo-ke, equivalent to a General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

sentences.zh: 分五部：曰內部，即漢桂婁部也，亦號黃部；

translations.literal: It is divided into five departments: called the Inner Department, which is the Han Guilou department, also called the Yellow Department;
translations.idiomatic: The realm is divided into five departments: the Inner Department, the old Han Guilou division, also called the Yellow Department;

sentences.zh: 曰北部，即絕奴部也，或號後部；

translations.literal: called the Northern Department, which is the Juedu department, or also called the Rear Department;
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Department, the Juedu division, sometimes called the Rear Department;

sentences.zh: 曰東部，即順奴部也，或號左部；

translations.literal: called the Eastern Department, which is the Shunnu department, or also called the Left Department;
translations.idiomatic: the Eastern Department, the Shunnu division, sometimes called the Left Department;

sentences.zh: 曰南部，即灌奴部也，亦號前部；

translations.literal: called the Southern Department, which is the Guannu department, also called the Front Department;
translations.idiomatic: the Southern Department, the Guannu division, also called the Front Department;

sentences.zh: 曰西部，即消奴部也。

translations.literal: called the Western Department, which is the Xiaonu department.
translations.idiomatic: and the Western Department, the Xiaonu division.

sentences.zh: 王服五采，以白羅制冠，革帶皆金扣。

translations.literal: The king wears five colors, with a crown made of white gauze, and leather belts all with gold clasps.
translations.idiomatic: The king wears robes of five colors, a crown of white gauze, and leather belts fitted with gold clasps.

sentences.zh: 大臣青羅冠，次絳羅，珥兩鳥羽，金銀雜扣，衫筒袖，褲大口，白韋帶，黃革履。

translations.literal: Ministers wear green gauze caps, next crimson gauze, with two bird feathers in the ears, gold and silver mixed clasps, jackets with tubular sleeves, trousers with wide legs, white leather belts, and yellow leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers wear green gauze caps—or crimson gauze as the next rank—with twin bird feathers at the ears, belts studded with gold and silver, jackets with narrow sleeves, wide-legged trousers, white leather belts, and yellow leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 庶人衣褐，戴弁。

translations.literal: Commoners wear brown cloth and wear caps.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners dress in brown cloth and wear simple caps.

sentences.zh: 女子首巾幗。

translations.literal: Women cover their heads with kerchiefs and headcloths.
translations.idiomatic: Women bind their hair with kerchiefs and headcloths.

sentences.zh: 俗喜弈、投壺、蹴鞠。

translations.literal: The custom favors chess, pitch-pot, and cuju.
translations.idiomatic: They are fond of chess, pitch-pot, and cuju ball games.

sentences.zh: 食用籩、豆、簠、簋、罍、洗。

translations.literal: For eating they use bian, dou, fu, gui, lei, and xi vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At meals they use the ritual vessels known as bian, dou, fu, gui, lei, and xi.

sentences.zh: 居依山谷，以草茨屋，惟王宮、官府、佛廬以瓦。

translations.literal: They dwell along valleys, thatching houses with grass; only the royal palace, government offices, and Buddhist halls use tile.
translations.idiomatic: They live in valleys and roof their homes with thatch; only the royal palace, government halls, and Buddhist temples are tiled.

sentences.zh: 窶民盛冬作長坑，煴火以取暖。

translations.literal: Poor people in deep winter dig long pits and bank fires for warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter the poor dig long pits and bank coals within them for heat.

sentences.zh: 其治，峭法以繩下，故少犯。

translations.literal: In their governance, severe law is applied with strictness, hence few offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Their government enforces harsh law without leniency, and so crime is rare.

sentences.zh: 叛者叢炬灼體，乃斬之，籍入其家。

translations.literal: Rebels are burned on heaps of torches over the body, then beheaded, and their households registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels are first scorched with piled torches, then beheaded, and their households are registered and their property seized.

sentences.zh: 降、敗、殺人及剽劫者斬，盜者十倍取償，殺牛馬者沒爲奴婢，故道不掇遺。

translations.literal: Deserters, defeated soldiers, murderers, and robbers are beheaded; thieves pay tenfold restitution; those who kill cattle or horses are confiscated as slaves; hence nothing is picked up on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters, defeated men, murderers, and bandits are beheaded; thieves must repay tenfold; anyone who kills cattle or horses is made a slave; and so nothing is left lying on the highways.

sentences.zh: 婚娶不用幣，有受者恥之。

translations.literal: Marriage takes no bride-price; to accept one is shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages require no bride-price; to accept one is considered disgraceful.

sentences.zh: 服父母喪三年，兄弟逾月除。

translations.literal: Mourning for parents lasts three years; for brothers, more than a month then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for parents lasts three years; for siblings, a little over a month.

sentences.zh: 俗多淫祠，禮靈星及日、箕子、可汗等神。

translations.literal: The custom has many excessive shrines, worshipping the Spirit Star, the Sun, Jizi, the Khaghan, and other spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They maintain many excessive shrines, sacrificing to the Spirit Star, the Sun, Jizi, the Khaghan, and other deities.

sentences.zh: 國左有大穴曰神隧，每十月，王皆自祭。

translations.literal: To the left of the state is a great cave called the Spirit Tunnel; every tenth month the king personally sacrifices there.
translations.idiomatic: East of the capital lies a great cavern called the Spirit Tunnel; each tenth month the king sacrifices there in person.

sentences.zh: 人喜學，至窮里廝家，亦相矜勉，衢側悉構嚴屋，號局堂，子弟未婚者曹處，誦經習射。

translations.literal: People delight in learning; even in poor lanes and servants' households they urge one another on; along the streets they all build solemn halls called Bureau Halls, where unmarried sons gather in groups to recite classics and practice archery.
translations.idiomatic: The people love learning; even in the poorest lanes and meanest households they urge one another on. Along every street they erect solemn halls called Bureau Halls, where unmarried youths gather to recite the classics and practice archery.

sentences.zh: 隋末，其王高元死，異母弟建武嗣。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, their king Gao Yuan died, and his younger brother by a different mother Jianwu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui dynasty their king Gao Yuan died, and his half-brother Jianwu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 武德初，再遣使入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he twice sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign he twice sent envoys to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 高祖下書脩好，約高麗人在中國者護送，中國人在高麗者敕遣還。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued a letter to restore good relations, agreeing that Goguryeo people in China would be escorted back, and Chinese in Goguryeo would be ordered to return.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent a letter restoring friendly relations, stipulating that Goguryeo subjects in China would be escorted home and Chinese subjects in Goguryeo would be ordered to return.

sentences.zh: 於是建武悉搜亡命歸有司，且萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jianwu searched out all fugitives and returned them to the authorities, nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu then hunted down fugitives and surrendered them to Tang authorities—nearly ten thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 後三年，遣使者拜爲上柱國、遼東郡王、高麗王。

translations.literal: Three years later, envoys were sent to invest him as Supreme Pillar of State, King of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the court sent envoys to invest him as Supreme Pillar of State, King of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 命道士以像法往，爲講《老子》。

translations.literal: A Daoist was ordered to go with image methods and lecture on the Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched a Daoist master to expound the Laozi by illustrated lecture.

sentences.zh: 建武大悅，率國人共聽之，日數千人。

translations.literal: Jianwu was greatly pleased and led the people of the state to listen together, several thousand daily.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu was delighted and led his people to attend; several thousand came each day.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「名實須相副。

translations.literal: The emperor said to those around him: "Title and reality must match.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attendants, "Titles and facts must correspond.

sentences.zh: 高麗雖臣于隋，而終拒煬帝，何臣之爲？

translations.literal: Goguryeo may have been subject to Sui, yet in the end it defied Emperor Yang—what sort of subjecthood is that?
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo may have submitted to the Sui, yet in the end it defied Emperor Yang—what kind of vassalage is that?

sentences.zh: 朕務安人，何必受其臣？」

translations.literal: I aim to settle the people—why must I accept them as subjects?"
translations.idiomatic: My aim is to bring peace to the people—why must I accept them as vassals?"

sentences.zh: 裴矩、溫彥博諫曰：「遼東本箕子國，魏晉時故封內，不可不臣。

translations.literal: Pei Ju and Wen Yanbo remonstrated: "Liaodong was originally the state of Jizi, within the old borders in Wei-Jin times—it cannot go unsubjected.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju and Wen Yanbo remonstrated, "Liaodong was originally Jizi's kingdom, within the old imperial domain since Wei and Jin—it cannot be left unsubmissive.

sentences.zh: 中國與夷狄，猶太陽於列星，不可以降。」

translations.literal: China and the barbarians are like the sun among the stars—one cannot lower oneself."
translations.idiomatic: China and the barbarians stand as the sun among the stars—our dignity cannot be lowered."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 明年，新羅、百濟上書，言建武閉道，使不得朝，且數侵入。

translations.literal: The next year Silla and Baekje submitted memorials saying Jianwu blocked the roads so their envoys could not attend court, and repeatedly invaded.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Silla and Baekje memorialized that Jianwu had closed the routes so their envoys could not reach court, and that he had repeatedly invaded their lands.

sentences.zh: 有詔散騎侍郎硃子奢持節諭和，建武謝罪，乃請與二國平。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Attendant Gentleman-at-Large Zhu Zishe to bear credentials and instruct reconciliation; Jianwu apologized and then asked to make peace with the two states.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Attendant Gentleman-at-Large Zhu Zishe as envoy to broker peace. Jianwu apologized and asked to settle with the two kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 太宗已禽突厥頡利，建武遣使者賀，并上封域圖。

translations.literal: When Taizong had already captured the Türk Jieli, Jianwu sent envoys to congratulate him and also submitted a map of his borders.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong captured the Türk khaghan Jieli, Jianwu sent envoys to congratulate him and submitted a map of his realm.

sentences.zh: 帝詔廣州司馬長孫師臨瘞隋士戰胔，毀高麗所立京觀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guangzhou Vice-Prefect Zhangsun Shi to go bury the corpses of Sui soldiers from battle and destroy the victory mounds Goguryeo had raised.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guangzhou Vice-Prefect Zhangsun Shi to bury the Sui war dead and tear down the victory mounds Goguryeo had erected.

sentences.zh: 建武懼，乃築長城千里，東北首扶餘，西南屬之海。

translations.literal: Jianwu was afraid and built a long wall of a thousand li, beginning in the northeast at Fuyu and in the southwest reaching the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Jianwu built a thousand-li wall from Fuyu in the northeast to the sea in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 久之，遣太子桓權入朝獻方物，帝厚賜齎，詔使者陳大德持節答勞，且觀亹。

translations.literal: After a long while he sent the crown prince Huanquan to court with tribute; the emperor richly rewarded him and ordered the envoy Chen Dade to bear credentials in reply and observe their strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: In time he sent Crown Prince Huanquan to court with tribute. The emperor lavished gifts upon him and dispatched Chen Dade with credentials to return the courtesy and observe the kingdom's strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 大德入其國，厚餉官守，悉得其纖曲。

translations.literal: Dade entered their state, richly rewarded the guarding officials, and learned all their minute details.
translations.idiomatic: Dade entered the kingdom, lavished gifts on the border officials, and learned every detail of their affairs.

sentences.zh: 見華人流客者，爲道親戚存亡，人人垂涕，故所至士女夾道觀。

translations.literal: When he saw Chinese sojourners he told them whether their kin were alive or dead, and everyone wept; hence wherever he went men and women lined the roads to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he met Chinese expatriates he told them news of their kin, alive or dead, and all wept; men and women lined the roads wherever he passed.

sentences.zh: 建武盛陳兵見使者。

translations.literal: Jianwu arrayed troops in force to receive the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu paraded a great host to receive the envoy.

sentences.zh: 大德還奏，帝悅。

translations.literal: Dade returned and reported; the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Dade returned and reported; the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 大德又言：「聞高昌滅，其大對廬三至館，有加禮焉。」

translations.literal: Dade also said: "I heard that when Gaochang fell, their Grand Tae-du-ru came three times to the lodge with added courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: Dade added, "When Gaochang fell, their Grand Tae-du-ru came three times to my lodging with special courtesy."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高麗地止四郡，我發卒數萬攻遼東，諸城必救，我以舟師自東萊帆海趨平壤，固易。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Goguryeo's territory is only four commanderies. If I send tens of thousands of troops to attack Liaodong, every city must come to the rescue; I would sail a fleet from Donglai across the sea to Pyongyang—that would be easy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Goguryeo holds only four commanderies' worth of land. Send tens of thousands against Liaodong and every city must rush to defend it; meanwhile a fleet from Donglai could sail straight to Pyongyang—that would be easy enough.

sentences.zh: 然天下甫平，不欲勞人耳。」

translations.literal: Yet the realm has only just been pacified—I do not wish to weary the people."
translations.idiomatic: But the realm has only just been pacified, and I do not wish to burden the people."

sentences.zh: 有蓋蘇文者，或號蓋金，姓泉氏，自云生水中以惑衆。

translations.literal: There was Gaisuwen, also called Gaijin, surname Quan, who claimed to have been born in the water to delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: There was Gaisuwen, also called Gaijin, of the Quan clan, who claimed to have been born in the water in order to beguile the people.

sentences.zh: 性忍暴。

translations.literal: By nature he was cruel and violent.
translations.idiomatic: He was cruel and violent by nature.

sentences.zh: 父爲東部大人、大對廬，死。

translations.literal: His father was Eastern Department chief and Grand Tae-du-ru, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been chief of the Eastern Department and Grand Tae-du-ru. When he died,

sentences.zh: 蓋蘇文當嗣，國人惡之，不得立。

translations.literal: Gaisuwen should have succeeded, but the people hated him and he could not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Gaisuwen should have succeeded him, but the people hated him and would not install him.

sentences.zh: 頓首謝衆，請攝職，有不可，雖廢無悔。

translations.literal: He kowtowed to thank the multitude, asked to hold the post provisionally, and said if it was not acceptable he would be removed without regret.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed to the assembly, begged to serve provisionally, and vowed that if they found him unfit they might remove him without his complaint.

sentences.zh: 衆哀之，遂嗣位。

translations.literal: The multitude pitied him, and he then succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, the people let him take the post.

sentences.zh: 殘凶不道，諸大臣與建武議誅之，蓋蘇文覺，悉召諸部，紿雲大閱兵，列饌具請大臣臨視，賓至盡殺之，凡百餘人。

translations.literal: Cruel and vicious beyond measure, the great ministers with Jianwu plotted to kill him; Gaisuwen learned of it, summoned all departments, deceived them saying there would be a great review of troops, set out feasts and invited the ministers to come view; when the guests arrived he killed them all, more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Savage and lawless, he drove the great ministers and Jianwu to plot his death. Gaisuwen learned of it, summoned every department, and announced a grand military review. He laid out a feast and invited the ministers to attend; when they arrived he slaughtered them all—more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 馳入宮殺建武，殘其屍投諸溝。

translations.literal: He galloped into the palace and killed Jianwu, mutilated his corpse, and threw it into a ditch.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped into the palace, killed Jianwu, mutilated the corpse, and cast it into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 更立建武弟之子藏爲王，自爲莫離支，專國，猶唐兵部尚書、中書令職云。

translations.literal: He set up Jianwu's younger brother's son Zang as king, made himself Mo-li-zhi and monopolized the state, like the Tang posts of Minister of War and Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He enthroned Jianwu's nephew Zang and made himself Mo-li-zhi, seizing sole power comparable to the Tang Minister of War and Director of the Secretariat combined.

sentences.zh: 貌魁秀，美須髯，冠服皆飾以金，佩五刀，左右莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and handsome, with a fine beard; crown and robes were all ornamented with gold; he wore five swords, and those beside him dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and handsome, with a splendid beard, he adorned crown and robes with gold, wore five swords at his belt, and none beside him dared raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 使貴人伏諸地，踐以升馬。

translations.literal: He made nobles lie on the ground and stepped on them to mount his horse.
translations.idiomatic: He made nobles prostrate themselves so he could step on their backs to mount his horse.

sentences.zh: 出入陳兵，長呼禁切，行人畏竄，至投坑穀。

translations.literal: Going in and out he arrayed troops, shouted long prohibitions, travelers feared and fled, even throwing themselves into pits and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad he marched with an armed escort, bellowing orders; travelers fled in terror, some even hurling themselves into pits and gullies.

sentences.zh: 帝聞建武爲下所殺，惻然遣使者持節弔祭。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Jianwu was killed by his subordinates and, moved to pity, sent an envoy with credentials to mourn and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jianwu had been murdered by his subjects, the emperor was moved to pity and sent an envoy with credentials to offer condolences and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 或勸帝可遂討之，帝不欲因喪伐罪，乃拜藏爲遼東郡王、高麗王。

translations.literal: Some urged the emperor that he could then attack; the emperor did not wish to punish a crime amid mourning and invested Zang as King of Liaodong Commandery and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged an immediate punitive campaign, but the emperor refused to strike during mourning and invested Zang as King of Liaodong Commandery and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蓋蘇文殺君攘國，朕取之易耳，不願勞人，若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Gaisuwen killed his lord and seized the state—I could take it easily, but I do not wish to weary the people—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Gaisuwen murdered his king and usurped the realm. I could seize it easily, yet I do not wish to burden the people—what should I do?"

sentences.zh: 司空房玄齡曰：「陛下士勇而力有餘，戢不用，所謂'止戈爲武'者。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Fang Xuanling said: "Your Majesty's soldiers are brave and strength remains in surplus; to sheath and not use them is what is called 'stopping the spear makes martial virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Fang Xuanling said, "Your soldiers are brave and your strength ample; to sheath the sword unused is the true meaning of martial virtue—‘to stop the spear is to be martial.’"

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫無忌曰：「高麗無一介告難，宜賜書安尉之，隱其患，撫其存，彼當聽命。」

translations.literal: Minister of Education Zhangsun Wuji said: "Goguryeo has not sent a single man to report distress; you should bestow a letter to comfort and reassure them, conceal their troubles, soothe those who remain, and they will heed orders."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Zhangsun Wuji said, "Goguryeo has sent no plea for help. Send a letter of reassurance, conceal their troubles, comfort the survivors, and they will submit."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 會新羅遣使者上書言：「高麗、百濟聯和，將見討。

translations.literal: It happened that Silla sent an envoy with a memorial saying: "Goguryeo and Baekje have joined forces and are about to attack us.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Silla sent an envoy with a memorial: "Goguryeo and Baekje have allied and are about to strike us.

sentences.zh: 謹歸命天子。」

translations.literal: We respectfully submit to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly place ourselves under the Son of Heaven's protection."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「若何而免？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How may you escape?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How can you be saved?"

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「計窮矣，惟陛下哀憐！」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Our plans are exhausted—only Your Majesty's pity!"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "We are at our wits' end—only Your Majesty's mercy can save us!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我以偏兵率契丹、靺鞨入遼東，而國可紓一歲，一策也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I could lead a detached force with the Khitan and Mohe into Liaodong, and your state could gain a year's relief—that is one plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I could send a detached force with Khitan and Mohe allies into Liaodong, giving your kingdom a year's respite—that is the first plan.

sentences.zh: 我以絳袍丹幟數千賜而國，至，建以陣，二國見，謂我師至，必走，二策也。

translations.literal: I could bestow several thousand crimson robes and red banners on your state; when they arrive, array them in formation—the two states will see them, think my army has come, and surely flee—that is the second plan.
translations.idiomatic: I could send you several thousand crimson robes and red banners; array them in battle order when they arrive, and the two kingdoms, thinking my army has come, will surely flee—that is the second plan.

sentences.zh: 百濟恃海，不修戎械，我以舟師數萬襲之；

translations.literal: Baekje relies on the sea and does not maintain arms; I could strike it with tens of thousands in a naval force;
translations.idiomatic: Baekje trusts to the sea and neglects its arms; I could strike it with a fleet of tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 而國女君，故爲鄰侮，我以宗室主而國，待安則自守之，三策也。

translations.literal: your state has a female ruler and is therefore bullied by neighbors; I could place a member of the imperial clan to rule your state, and when settled you would guard yourselves—that is the third plan.
translations.idiomatic: your kingdom has a queen regnant and is therefore bullied by neighbors; I could install a prince of the imperial clan to rule you, and once secure you could defend yourselves—that is the third plan.

sentences.zh: 使者計孰取？」

translations.literal: Envoy, which plan do you take?"
translations.idiomatic: Envoy, which of these plans do you choose?"

sentences.zh: 使者不能對。

translations.literal: The envoy could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy had no answer.

sentences.zh: 於是遣司農丞相里玄獎以璽書讓高麗，且使止勿攻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Bolizhi Xuanjiang, Minister of Agriculture, with an imperial letter bearing the seal to reproach Goguryeo and also to order them to cease attacking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Bolizhi Xuanjiang, Minister of Agriculture, with a sealed imperial missive rebuking Goguryeo and commanding them to halt their attack.

sentences.zh: 使未至，而蓋蘇文已取新羅二城。

translations.literal: Before the envoy arrived, Gaisuwen had already taken two cities of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy arrived, Gaisuwen had already seized two Silla cities.

sentences.zh: 玄獎諭帝旨，答曰：「往隋見侵，新羅乘邅奪我地五百里，今非盡反地，兵不止。」

translations.literal: Xuanjiang conveyed the emperor's command; they replied: "In the past we were invaded by the Sui; Silla seized our moment of distress to wrest five hundred li of our territory; unless all the land is returned, the army will not stop."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjiang delivered the emperor's message. They answered, "The Sui invaded us in former times, and Silla seized our distress to snatch five hundred li of our land. Unless every inch is returned, our armies will not cease."

sentences.zh: 玄獎曰：「往事烏足論邪？

translations.literal: Xuanjiang said: "Past affairs—how are they worth discussing?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjiang said, "Why dwell on past grievances?

sentences.zh: 遼東故中國郡縣，天子且不取，高麗焉得違詔？」

translations.literal: Liaodong was formerly the commanderies and counties of China; the Son of Heaven does not even take it—how may Goguryeo defy the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong was once Chinese territory. The Son of Heaven himself does not claim it—how dare Goguryeo defy his command?"

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: They would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: They refused.

sentences.zh: 玄獎還奏，帝曰：「莫離支殺君，虐用其下如擭阱，怨痛溢道，我出師無名哉？」

translations.literal: Xuanjiang returned and reported. The emperor said: "Moryangji killed his lord and cruelly used his subordinates as snare-traps; resentment and pain overflow the roads—would my campaign be without just cause?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjiang reported back. The emperor said, "Moryangji murdered his king and tormented his people like beasts in a trap. Grievance fills every road—how can my campaign lack just cause?"

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良曰：「陛下之兵度遼而克固善，萬分一不得逞，且再用師，再用師，安危不可億。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance Secretariat Counselor Chu Suiliang said: "If Your Majesty's army crosses the Liao and conquers, that is surely well; but if in one case in ten thousand it does not succeed, and troops are used again and yet again, security cannot be reckoned."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Secretariat Counselor Chu Suiliang said, "If your army crosses the Liao and triumphs, all is well—but if there is even one chance in ten thousand of failure, and you must march again and again, the realm's safety becomes incalculable."

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書李勣曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Minister of War Li Ji said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Li Ji said, "I disagree.

sentences.zh: 曩薛延陀盜邊，陛下欲追擊，魏徵苦諫而止。

translations.literal: Formerly when Xueyantuo raided the frontier, Your Majesty wished to pursue and strike; Wei Zheng strenuously remonstrated and you stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueyantuo raided the borderlands, Your Majesty wished to pursue them, but Wei Zheng remonstrated forcefully and you desisted.

sentences.zh: 向若擊之，一馬不生返。

translations.literal: Had you struck then, not a single horse would have returned alive.
translations.idiomatic: Had you attacked then, not one horse would have come home.

sentences.zh: 後復畔擾，至今爲恨。」

translations.literal: Later they rebelled and harassed again—to this day it remains a regret."
translations.idiomatic: They rebelled and raided again thereafter—a regret that haunts us still."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is true.

sentences.zh: 但一慮之失而尤之，後誰爲我計者？」

translations.literal: But if one failure of deliberation is blamed, who afterward will plan for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if every cautious doubt is punished, who will dare counsel me in the future?"

sentences.zh: 新羅數請援，乃下吳船四百柁輸糧，詔營州都督張儉等發幽、營兵及契丹、奚、靺鞨等出討。

translations.literal: Silla repeatedly requested aid; thereupon four hundred Wu ships were dispatched to transport grain, and an edict ordered Protector-General of Yingzhou Zhang Jian and others to mobilize Youzhou and Yingzhou troops and Khitan, Xi, Mohe, and others to march out in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Silla pleaded for aid again and again. The court dispatched four hundred Wu ships loaded with grain and ordered Zhang Jian, Protector-General of Yingzhou, to lead troops from Youzhou and Yingzhou together with Khitan, Xi, Mohe, and others on a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 會遼溢，師還。

translations.literal: The Liao overflowed its banks; the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao River flooded, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 莫離支懼，遣使者內金，帝不納。

translations.literal: Moryangji was afraid and sent envoys to present gold; the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Moryangji grew fearful and sent envoys bearing tribute gold, but the emperor refused it.

sentences.zh: 使者又言：「莫離支遣官五十入宿衛。」

translations.literal: The envoys also said: "Moryangji has sent fifty officials to enter palace guard service."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys added, "Moryangji wishes to send fifty officials to serve in the palace guard."

sentences.zh: 帝怒責使者曰：「而等委質高武，而不伏節死義，又爲逆子謀，不可赦。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily reproached the envoys: "You pledged yourselves to King Gao yet failed to uphold loyalty and die for righteousness, and now you scheme for the rebel son—you cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked them in wrath: "You submitted to King Gao yet failed to die for your sovereign. Now you conspire for his murderer's son. There is no pardon for you."

sentences.zh: 悉下之獄。

translations.literal: All were cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of them was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 於是帝欲自將討之，召長安耆老勞曰：「遼東故中國地，而莫離支賊殺其主，朕將自行經略之，故與父老約：子若孫從我行者，我能拊循之，毋庸恤也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor wished to lead the campaign in person; he summoned the elders of Chang'an and comforted them, saying: "Liaodong is former territory of China, and Moryangji treacherously killed his lord; I shall personally go to take command. I make this pledge with you, fathers and elders: if sons or grandsons march with me, I can comfort and tend them—you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resolved to lead the campaign himself. He summoned Chang'an's elders and told them, "Liaodong was once Chinese soil, and Moryangji murdered his king. I will command the campaign in person. I give you my word, elders: if your sons or grandsons march with me, I will see to their welfare. You have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 即厚賜布粟。

translations.literal: He immediately bestowed bountiful gifts of cloth and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He then lavished cloth and grain upon them.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆勸帝毋行，帝曰：「吾知之矣，去本而就末，舍高以取下，釋近而之遠，三者爲不祥，伐高麗是也。

translations.literal: The ministers all urged the emperor not to go. The emperor said: "I know it already: to leave the root and pursue the branch tip, to abandon the high and take the low, to release what is near and go to what is far—these three are inauspicious; campaigning against Goguryeo is exactly such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all urged the emperor to stay. He said, "I know the objections: abandoning the root for the branch, forsaking the heights for the low ground, leaving the near to strike the far—these three are ill omens, and a campaign against Goguryeo fits them all.

sentences.zh: 然蓋蘇文弑君，又戮大臣以逞，一國之人延頸待救，議者顧未亮耳。」

translations.literal: Yet Gaisuwen murdered his lord and slaughtered great ministers to impose his will; the people of the whole state crane their necks awaiting rescue—those who debate simply have not seen clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaisuwen killed his king and butchered his ministers to have his way. The entire kingdom waits with bared necks for deliverance. The court simply does not see it clearly."

sentences.zh: 於是北輸粟營州，東儲粟古大人城。

translations.literal: Thereupon grain was transported north to Yingzhou, and grain was stored east at Gudaducheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was shipped north to Yingzhou and stockpiled east at Gudaducheng.

sentences.zh: 帝幸洛陽，乃以張亮爲平壤道行軍大總管，常何、左難當副之，冉仁德、劉英行、張文幹、龐孝泰、程名振爲總管，帥江、吳、京、洛募兵凡四萬，吳艘五百，泛海趨平壤。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Luoyang and appointed Zhang Liang Grand Marshal of the Pyongyang Route Army, with Chang He and Zuo Nandang as deputies and Ran Rende, Liu Yingxing, Zhang Wengan, Pang Xiaotai, and Cheng Mingzhen as commanders; he led forty thousand recruited troops from the Jiang, Wu, Jing, and Luo regions, five hundred Wu ships, crossing the sea toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Luoyang and made Zhang Liang Grand Marshal of the Pyongyang Route, with Chang He and Zuo Nandang as his deputies and Ran Rende, Liu Yingxing, Zhang Wengan, Pang Xiaotai, and Cheng Mingzhen as subordinate commanders. He led forty thousand recruits from the Jiang, Wu, Jing, and Luo regions aboard five hundred Wu ships, sailing by sea toward Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 以李勣爲遼東道行軍大總管，江夏王道宗副之，張士貴、張儉、執失思力、契苾何力、阿史那彌射、薑德本、曲智盛、吳黑闥爲行軍總管隸之，帥騎士六萬趨遼東。

translations.literal: Li Ji was made Grand Marshal of the Liaodong Route Army, with the Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong as deputy; Zhang Shigui, Zhang Jian, Zhishi Sili, Qibi Heli, Ashina Mishe, Jiang Deben, Qu Zhisheng, and Wu Heita were made campaign commanders subordinate to him; he led sixty thousand horsemen toward Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji was appointed Grand Marshal of the Liaodong Route, with Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong as his deputy. Zhang Shigui, Zhang Jian, Zhishi Sili, Qibi Heli, Ashina Mishe, Jiang Deben, Qu Zhisheng, and Wu Heita served under him as campaign commanders, leading sixty thousand cavalry toward Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕所過，營頓毋飭，食毋豐怪，水可涉者勿作橋樑，行在非近州縣不得令學生、耆老迎謁。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Where I pass, camps and halts are not to be adorned; food is not to be lavish and strange; where water can be waded, do not build bridges; where the mobile court is not near a prefecture or county, do not order students and elders to come welcome and attend.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Along my route, camps must not be lavishly prepared, nor food extravagantly supplied. Where water can be forded, build no bridges. Where the mobile court does not halt near a prefecture or county, do not summon students or elders to greet me.

sentences.zh: 朕昔提戈撥亂，無盈月儲，猶所響風靡。

translations.literal: I formerly took spear in hand to quell disorder; we had not a full month's stores, yet wherever we turned, the wind laid all low.
translations.idiomatic: When I first took up arms to end the chaos, we had less than a month's provisions—yet wherever we marched, enemies fell like grass before the wind.

sentences.zh: 今幸家給人足，只恐勞於轉餉，故驅牛羊以飼軍。

translations.literal: Now fortunately families are provided for and people have enough—I only fear weariness in forwarding supplies; therefore I drive cattle and sheep to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is prosperous, but I fear the burden of supply trains—so I drive cattle and sheep along to feed the army on the march.

sentences.zh: 且朕必勝有五：以我大擊彼小，以我順討彼逆，以我安乘彼亂，以我逸敵彼勞，以我悅當彼怨，渠憂不克邪！」

translations.literal: Moreover I am sure of victory in five ways: with my greatness I strike their smallness; with my righteousness I punish their rebellion; with my security I ride their disorder; with my rest I meet their exhaustion; with my people's contentment I face their resentment—why worry that we cannot conquer!"
translations.idiomatic: I have five reasons for certain victory: we are great and they are small; we are righteous and they are rebellious; we are secure and they are in turmoil; we are rested and they are weary; our people are content and theirs are resentful—how can we fail to conquer!"

sentences.zh: 又發契丹、奚、新羅、百濟諸君長兵悉會。

translations.literal: Troop levies from the Khitan, Xi, Silla, Baekje, and other tribal chiefs were all mobilized to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from the Khitan, Xi, Silla, Baekje, and other allied chiefs were also mobilized to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，帝自洛陽次定州，謂左右曰：「今天下大定，唯遼東未賓，後嗣因士馬盛強，謀臣導以征討，喪亂方始，朕故自取之，不遺後世憂也。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year, the emperor left Luoyang and halted at Dingzhou; he said to those at his side: "Today the realm is broadly settled; only Liaodong has not submitted. Later generations, because troops and horses are strong, with strategists guiding them toward campaigns of conquest—disorder would just begin—therefore I personally take this, not to bequeath worry to posterity."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year, the emperor left Luoyang and halted at Dingzhou. He told his attendants, "The realm is now at peace, but Liaodong remains unsubdued. Future rulers, emboldened by strong armies and urged on by strategists, would launch campaigns that bring ruin just as it begins. I take this burden upon myself so that posterity need not suffer it."

sentences.zh: 帝坐城門，過兵，人人撫慰，疾病者親視之，敕州縣治療，士大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor sat at the city gate; as troops passed, he comforted each man; for the sick he viewed them personally and ordered prefectures and counties to treat them; the soldiers were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat at the city gate as the troops marched past, comforting each soldier in turn. He personally inspected the sick and ordered local officials to treat them. The army was deeply heartened.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌白奏：「天下符魚悉從，而宮官止十人，天下以爲輕神器。」

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji reported in person: "Throughout the realm the tallies of office all follow, yet palace attendants number only ten—the realm thinks you hold the sacred regalia lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji reported in person, "All the empire's seals and insignia accompany you, yet your palace attendants number only ten. The realm fears you hold the throne too lightly."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「士度遼十萬，皆去家室。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A hundred thousand soldiers cross the Liao—all have left their homes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A hundred thousand men are crossing the Liao, every one of them far from home.

sentences.zh: 朕以十人從，尚恧其多，公止勿言！」

translations.literal: I have only ten men following me and am already ashamed it is so many—minister, say no more!"
translations.idiomatic: I bring only ten attendants and am already ashamed that is so many. Say no more of it!"

sentences.zh: 帝身屬橐房，結兩箙於鞍。

translations.literal: The emperor personally carried the quiver, tying two arrow cases to the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor carried his own quiver and tied two arrow cases to his saddle.

sentences.zh: 四月，勣績濟遼水，高麗皆嬰城守。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Li Ji's wing crossed the Liao River; Goguryeo all held their cities in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Li Ji led his forces across the Liao River. Every Goguryeo city shut its gates and prepared to resist.

sentences.zh: 帝大饗士，帳幽州之南，詔長孫無忌誓師，乃引而東。

translations.literal: The emperor gave a great feast to the troops with encampment south of Youzhou; he ordered Zhangsun Wuji to rally the army with oaths, then led them eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted the army with his camp south of Youzhou, had Zhangsun Wuji administer the oath of mobilization, and then led the host eastward.

sentences.zh: 勣攻蓋牟城，拔之，得戶二萬，糧十萬石，以其地爲蓋州。

translations.literal: Li Ji attacked Gaemou City, took it, obtained twenty thousand households and a hundred thousand shi of grain, and made the territory into Gai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji attacked Gaemou City and captured it, taking twenty thousand households and a hundred thousand shi of grain. The territory was organized as Gai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 程名振攻沙卑城，夜入其西，城潰，虜其口八千，遊兵鴨淥上。

translations.literal: Cheng Mingzhen attacked Sabiei City; at night he entered its west; the city collapsed; he captured eight thousand persons; detached troops ranged on the Yalu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Mingzhen attacked Sabiei City, entering its western quarter by night. The city fell, and he took eight thousand captives. Detached troops then ranged along the Yalu River.

sentences.zh: 勣遂圍遼東城。

translations.literal: Li Ji then besieged Liaodong City.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji then laid siege to Liaodong City.

sentences.zh: 帝次遼澤，詔瘞隋戰士露骼。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at Liaomarsh and ordered burial of the Sui warriors' exposed bones.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted at Liaomarsh and ordered the burial of Sui soldiers whose bones lay exposed on the field.

sentences.zh: 高麗發新城、國內城騎四萬救遼東。

translations.literal: Goguryeo dispatched forty thousand horsemen from Xincheng and Gungnae to relieve Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo sent forty thousand cavalry from Xincheng and Gungnae to relieve Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 道宗率張乂君逆戰，君乂卻。

translations.literal: Daozong led Zhang Yijun to meet them in battle; Yijun retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong led Zhang Yijun to intercept them, but Yijun fell back.

sentences.zh: 道宗以騎馳之，虜兵辟易，奪其梁，收散卒，高以望，見高麗陣囂，急擊破之，斬首千餘級，誅君乂以徇。

translations.literal: Daozong galloped with his cavalry; the enemy troops gave way; he seized their ford, gathered scattered soldiers, ascended high to look, saw the Goguryeo formation in uproar, and swiftly struck and broke them, beheading more than a thousand; he executed Yijun to display as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong charged with his cavalry. The enemy gave way, and he seized their crossing, rallied the scattered troops, and climbed a height to survey the field. Seeing the Goguryeo line in disorder, he pressed the attack and broke them, taking more than a thousand heads. He executed Yijun as an example to the army.

sentences.zh: 帝度遼水，徹杠彴，堅士心。

translations.literal: The emperor crossed the Liao River, removed the bridges, and steadied the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed the Liao River, had the bridges dismantled behind him, and thereby steeled the army's resolve.

sentences.zh: 營馬首山，身到城下，見士填塹，分負之，重者馬上持之'群臣震懼，爭挾塊以進。

translations.literal: He encamped at Horse Head Mountain, went in person to below the wall, saw soldiers filling the moat, shared the carrying of earth, and for heavy loads held them on horseback; the ministers were shaken with fear and vied to seize lumps of earth and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong encamped at Horse Head Mountain and went in person to the foot of the wall. Seeing soldiers filling the moat, he shared the burden—lighter loads he carried himself, heavier ones he bore from horseback. The courtiers were terrified and competed to lug earth forward themselves.

sentences.zh: 城有硃蒙祠，祠有鎖甲、銛矛，妄言前燕世天所降。

translations.literal: The city had a shrine to Jumong; in the shrine were locked armor and sharp spears, falsely said to have been sent down from Heaven in Former Yan times.
translations.idiomatic: The city held a shrine to Jumong, where locked armor and keen spears were kept—falsely claimed to have descended from Heaven in the age of Former Yan.

sentences.zh: 方圍急，飾美女以婦神，誣言硃蒙悅，城必完。

translations.literal: As the siege pressed tight, they adorned beautiful women as the Bride Goddess, falsely saying Jumong was pleased and the city would surely be secure.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened, they dressed beautiful women as the Bride Goddess and spread the lie that Jumong was pleased and the city would surely hold.

sentences.zh: 勣列拋車，飛大石過三百步，所當輒潰，虜積木爲樓，結絙罔，不能拒。

translations.literal: Li Shiji deployed trebuchets; great stones flew more than three hundred paces, and whatever they struck at once collapsed; the enemy piled wood to make towers and knotted rope nets but could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji lined up trebuchets whose stones flew more than three hundred paces, shattering whatever they hit. The enemy raised wooden towers and rope netting but could not hold them off.

sentences.zh: 以沖車撞陴屋，碎之。

translations.literal: They used battering rams to strike the parapet structures and shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: Battering rams smashed the parapet works to pieces.

sentences.zh: 時百濟上金旐鎧，又以玄金爲山五文鎧，士被以從。

translations.literal: At the time Baekje presented golden-banner armor, and also made mountain-pattern five-motif armor of dark gold; the soldiers wore them and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje had sent golden-banner armor, and dark-gold mountain-pattern armor with five motifs; the troops wore these and marched on.

sentences.zh: 帝與勣會，甲光炫日。

translations.literal: The emperor and Li Shiji joined forces; the gleam of armor dazzled the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong and Li Shiji united their forces, and the flash of armor blazed in the sunlight.

sentences.zh: 會南風急，士縱火焚西南，熛延城中，屋幾盡，人死于燎者萬餘。

translations.literal: Just then a strong south wind blew; the soldiers set fire in the southwest; flames spread through the city; buildings were nearly all consumed, and more than ten thousand people died in the blaze.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce south wind sprang up; the troops fired the southwest quarter, and flames raced through the city until scarcely a building remained. More than ten thousand perished in the conflagration.

sentences.zh: 衆登陴，虜蒙盾以拒，士舉長矛舂之，藺石如雨，城遂潰，獲勝兵萬，戶四萬，糧五十萬石。

translations.literal: The masses climbed the battlements; the enemy covered themselves with shields to resist; soldiers raised long spears and rammed them; bundled stones fell like rain; the city then breached; they captured ten thousand picked troops, forty thousand households, and five hundred thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The army scaled the walls; the defenders hid behind shields while Tang spearmen battered them down and sling-stones fell like rain. The city gave way. They took ten thousand elite troops, forty thousand households, and five hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 以其地爲遼州。

translations.literal: They made that territory Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That territory was organized as Liao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，帝自太子所屬行在，舍置一烽，約下遼東舉烽，是日傳燎入塞。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at the mobile camp attached to the crown prince's establishment, he had set up a beacon and agreed that when Liaodong raised a beacon it would be done; on that day the signal fire was relayed into the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Taizong was at the crown prince's mobile camp, he had set out a beacon and arranged that Liaodong would light one at victory; that day the blaze was relayed through the passes into the interior.

sentences.zh: 進攻白崖城，城負山有厓水，險甚。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Baiya City; the city leaned against the mountain with a cliff and water, exceedingly perilous.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack on Baiya City, which clung to a mountain above a cliff-girded river—terrain of the gravest danger.

sentences.zh: 帝壁西北。

translations.literal: The emperor fortified the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong entrenched the northwest.

sentences.zh: 虜酋孫伐音陰丐降，然城中不能一。

translations.literal: The barbarian chief Sun Fayin secretly begged to surrender, yet within the city they could not unite.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy chief Sun Fayin secretly sought to surrender, but the city could not agree as one.

sentences.zh: 帝賜幟曰：「若降，建於堞以信。」

translations.literal: The emperor gave him a banner and said: "If you surrender, raise it on the parapet as a pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong gave him a banner and said, "If you mean to surrender, plant this on the parapet as your pledge."

sentences.zh: 俄而舉幟，城人皆以唐兵登矣，乃降。

translations.literal: Before long the banner was raised; the people in the city all thought Tang troops had climbed the wall, and then they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the banner went up; the townspeople all believed Tang soldiers were already on the walls, and they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，伐音中悔，帝怒，約以虜口畀諸將。

translations.literal: At first Fayin reconsidered midway; the emperor was angry and stipulated that the barbarian captives be given to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Fayin had wavered at first, and Taizong, enraged, had promised the captives to his generals as booty.

sentences.zh: 及是，李勣曰：「士奮而先，貪虜獲也。

translations.literal: When this happened, Li Shiji said: "The troops are striving to be first, greedy for barbarian captives.
translations.idiomatic: Now Li Shiji said, "The men are fighting to get ahead—they hunger for captives.

sentences.zh: 今城危拔，不可許降以孤士心。」

translations.literal: Now that the city is perilously about to be taken, we cannot allow surrender and thus chill the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The city is on the verge of falling; we cannot accept a surrender now and leave the soldiers empty-handed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「將軍言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The general speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "The general is right.

sentences.zh: 然縱兵殺戮，略人妻孥，朕不忍。

translations.literal: Yet to let the army slaughter, seize people's wives and children—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to let the army butcher them and seize their wives and children—that I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 將軍麾下有功者，朕能以庫物賞之，庶因將軍贖一城乎。」

translations.literal: For those under the general's command who have merit, I can reward them with treasury goods—might we thereby, through the general, redeem a city?"
translations.idiomatic: Those under your command who have earned merit I can reward from the treasury—might we, through you, ransom this one city?"

sentences.zh: 獲男女凡萬、兵二千。

translations.literal: They took men and women totaling ten thousand and two thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: They took ten thousand men and women altogether and two thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 以其地爲岩州，拜伐音爲刺史。

translations.literal: They made that territory Yan Prefecture and appointed Fayin regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: That territory became Yan Prefecture, and Fayin was appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 莫離支以加屍人七百戍蓋牟，勣俘之。

translations.literal: Gaisuwen had seven hundred Gasir people garrison Gaimou; Li Shiji captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaisuwen had posted seven hundred Gasir tribesmen to garrison Gaimou; Li Shiji took them prisoner.

sentences.zh: 請自效，帝曰：「而家加屍，乃爲我戰，將盡戮矣。

translations.literal: They asked to serve of their own accord; the emperor said: "Your clans are Gasir—yet you fight for me; I should slaughter you all.
translations.idiomatic: They offered to serve willingly. Taizong said, "You are Gasir by clan, yet you fight for me—I ought to execute every one of you.

sentences.zh: 夷一姓求一人力，不可。」

translations.literal: To exterminate one surname for the sake of one man's strength—is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: To wipe out a whole clan for one man's strength—that I will not do."

sentences.zh: 稟而縱之。

translations.literal: He received their plea and released them.
translations.idiomatic: He heard their petition and let them go.

sentences.zh: 次安市。

translations.literal: Next they went to Ansi.
translations.idiomatic: Next they marched on Ansi.

sentences.zh: 於是高麗北部傉薩高延壽、南部傉薩高惠真引兵及靺鞨衆十五萬來援。

translations.literal: Thereupon Goguryeo's northern irgan Gao Yanshou and southern irgan Gao Huizhen led troops together with Mohe forces, a hundred and fifty thousand in all, to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Then Goguryeo's northern irgan Gao Yanshou and southern irgan Gao Huizhen marched to the relief with Mohe allies—one hundred fifty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼若勒兵連安市而壁，據高山，取城中粟食之，縱靺鞨略吾牛馬，攻之不可下，此上策也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If they hold their army, link with Ansi and fortify themselves, occupy the high mountains, take grain from the city to eat, and let the Mohe harass our oxen and horses—then it could not be taken by assault; that would be the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "If they mass their troops, join Ansi, and entrench on the heights—living off the city's grain while the Mohe harry our cattle and horses—we could not bring them down. That would be their best plan.

sentences.zh: 拔城夜去，中策也。

translations.literal: To abandon the city and withdraw by night would be the middling plan.
translations.idiomatic: To slip away from the city by night would be the middling plan.

sentences.zh: 與吾爭鋒，則禽矣。」

translations.literal: To cross blades with us—they will be captured.
translations.idiomatic: To meet us in open battle—they will be ours."

sentences.zh: 有大對廬爲延壽計曰：「吾聞中國亂，豪雄並奮，秦王神武，敵無堅，戰無前，遂定天下，南面而帝，北狄、西戎罔不臣。

translations.literal: A Grand Dulü devised a plan for Yanshou, saying: "I have heard that when China was in turmoil heroes arose together; the Prince of Qin was divine in war—no enemy stood firm against him, no battle did he not win—and so he settled the realm and faced south as emperor; northern Di and western Rong, none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: A grand dulü counseled Yanshou: "When China was torn by chaos, heroes rose on every side—but the Prince of Qin was a god of war. No foe stood before him, no battle did he lose. He pacified the realm and took the throne facing south; north and west, none refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 今掃地而來，謀臣重將皆在，其鋒不可校。

translations.literal: Now he sweeps the ground coming; his strategists and great generals are all present—their edge cannot be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Now he sweeps across the land with every strategist and seasoned general at his side. Their edge cannot be matched.

sentences.zh: 今莫若頓兵曠日，陰遣奇兵絕其餉道，不旬月糧盡，欲戰不得，歸則無路，乃可取也。」

translations.literal: Now it would be best to hold the army for days on end and secretly send picked troops to cut their supply route; in less than ten months grain will be exhausted—they will wish to fight but cannot, and if they return there will be no road—then they can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold our ground for weeks and send picked men in secret to sever their supply line. Within ten months their grain will be gone—they will want to fight but cannot; if they retreat, they will have no road home. Then we can take them."

sentences.zh: 延壽不從，引軍距安市四十里而屯。

translations.literal: Yanshou did not follow this, led his army to forty li from Ansi and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou would not heed him. He drew up his army forty li from Ansi and made camp.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「虜墮吾策中矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The barbarians have fallen into my stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "The enemy has walked into my trap."

sentences.zh: 命左衛大將軍阿史那社爾以突厥千騎嘗之，虜常以靺鞨銳兵居前，社爾兵接而北。

translations.literal: He ordered Left Guard General Ashina She'er to test them with a thousand Turkic horsemen; the enemy customarily placed Mohe crack troops in the van; She'er's men engaged and then retreated north.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Left Guard General Ashina She'er to probe them with a thousand Turk horsemen. The enemy habitually put Mohe shock troops in the van; She'er's men skirmished and then feigned retreat northward.

sentences.zh: 延壽曰：「唐易與耳。」

translations.literal: Yanshou said: "Tang is easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou said, "Tang will be easy to handle."

sentences.zh: 進一舍，倚麓而陣。

translations.literal: He advanced one stage and arrayed his troops leaning on the foothills.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward one day's march and formed his battle line along the foothills.

sentences.zh: 帝詔延壽曰：「我以爾有強臣賊殺其主，來問罪，即交戰，非我意。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent word to Yanshou: "Because you had a powerful minister who murdered his lord as a traitor, I came to inquire into the crime—immediate battle is not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent word to Yanshou: "I came because a powerful minister of yours murdered his king in treason—to demand an accounting. To fight at once was never my wish."

sentences.zh: 延壽謂然，按甲俟。

translations.literal: Yanshou thought this plausible and held his armor waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou found this plausible and held his troops in check, waiting.

sentences.zh: 帝夜召諸將，使李勣率步騎萬五千陣西嶺當賊，長孫無忌、牛進達精兵萬人出虜背狹穀，帝以騎四千偃幟趨虜北山上，令諸軍曰：「聞鼓聲而縱。」

translations.literal: That night the emperor summoned the generals, had Li Shiji lead fifteen thousand infantry and cavalry to form battle lines on the western ridge to face the enemy, Zhangsun Wuji and Niu Jinda with ten thousand elite troops to emerge through the narrow valley behind the enemy's back; the emperor with four thousand horsemen hid banners and hastened to the enemy's north mountain, and ordered all armies: "When you hear the drum, charge.
translations.idiomatic: That night Taizong called his generals. Li Shiji was to take fifteen thousand foot and horse and form on the western ridge to face the enemy; Zhangsun Wuji and Niu Jinda, with ten thousand picked troops, were to slip through the narrow gorge behind the enemy; Taizong himself, with four thousand cavalry and banners lowered, would climb the mountain north of the foe. He ordered every unit: "At the drum, charge."

sentences.zh: 張幄朝堂，曰：「明日日中，納降虜於此。」

translations.literal: He pitched a canopy like a court hall and said: "Tomorrow at midday I will receive surrendering captives here."
translations.idiomatic: He raised a pavilion like a throne hall and said, "Tomorrow at noon I will receive the surrendered enemy here."

sentences.zh: 是夜，流星墮延壽營。

translations.literal: That night a meteor fell into Yanshou's camp.
translations.idiomatic: That night a meteor fell into Yanshou's camp.

sentences.zh: 旦日，虜視勣軍少，即戰。

translations.literal: At dawn the barbarians saw Li Shiji's army was small and immediately gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy saw Li Shiji's force was small and attacked at once.

sentences.zh: 帝望無忌軍塵上，命鼓角作，兵幟四合，虜惶惑，將分兵禦之，衆已囂。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Wuji's army dust rising, ordered drums and horns sounded, military banners closed in from four sides; the barbarians were alarmed and confused; they were about to divide troops to resist, but the host was already in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw the dust of Wuji's column rising, ordered drums and horns, and banners closed in from every side. The enemy panicked; they were about to split their force to meet the threat, but their ranks were already in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 勣以步槊擊敗之，無忌乘其後，帝自山馳下，虜大亂，斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: Li Shiji with infantry spears struck and defeated them; Wuji followed from behind; the emperor charged down from the mountain; the barbarians fell into great disorder; twenty thousand heads were severed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji broke them with infantry spears; Wuji struck from the rear; Taizong charged down the mountain. The enemy collapsed in chaos, and twenty thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 延壽收餘衆負山自固，無忌、勣合圍之，徹川梁，斷歸路。

translations.literal: Yanshou gathered the remnant troops, relied on the mountain to hold firm; Wuji and Li Shiji jointly encircled them, tore up the river bridges, and cut off the road of return.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou rallied his survivors and clung to the mountain to make a stand. Wuji and Li Shiji closed the ring around him, tore up the river bridges, and severed his retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝按轡觀虜營壘曰：「高麗傾國來，一麾而破，天贊我也。」

translations.literal: The emperor held the reins and viewed the barbarian camps and ramparts, saying: "Goguryeo came with the whole nation, yet one wave of the hand and they are broken—Heaven aids me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong reined in his horse and surveyed the enemy camps and walls. "Goguryeo threw its whole kingdom against us," he said, "and one gesture of my hand broke them. Heaven is on my side."

sentences.zh: 下馬再拜，謝況于天。

translations.literal: He dismounted and bowed twice, giving thanks to Heaven for this circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and bowed twice, giving thanks to Heaven for this turn of fortune.

sentences.zh: 延壽等度勢窮，即舉衆降。

translations.literal: Yanshou and the others, seeing their situation exhausted, then raised the host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanshou and his fellows, seeing their position hopeless, surrendered with their entire force.

sentences.zh: 入轅門，膝而前，拜手請命。

translations.literal: Entering the barbican gate, they advanced on their knees, bowed with folded hands, and begged for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the barbican gate and crawled forward on their knees, hands folded in supplication, begging for mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「後敢與天子戰乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Will you dare fight the Son of Heaven again?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Would you dare take the field against the Son of Heaven again?"

sentences.zh: 惶汗不得對。

translations.literal: In terror and sweating they could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Trembling and drenched in sweat, they could not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝料酋長三千五百人，悉官之，許內徙，餘衆三萬縱還之，誅靺鞨三千餘人，獲馬牛十萬，明光鎧萬領。

translations.literal: The emperor selected three thousand five hundred chieftains, gave them all office, permitted relocation within [the empire], released the remaining thirty thousand to return, executed more than three thousand Mohe, and took one hundred thousand horses and cattle and ten thousand suits of bright armor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong singled out three thousand five hundred chieftains, gave them all posts, and allowed them to resettle within the empire. He sent the other thirty thousand men home, executed more than three thousand Mohe auxiliaries, and seized a hundred thousand horses and cattle and ten thousand suits of gleaming armor.

sentences.zh: 高麗震駭，後黃、銀二城自拔去，數百里無舍煙。

translations.literal: Goguryeo was struck with terror; the two cities of Houhuang and Yin withdrew of themselves, and for several hundred li there was no smoke from dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo was shaken with fear. The cities of Houhuang and Yin abandoned themselves to the Tang, and for hundreds of li not a wisp of hearth smoke showed.

sentences.zh: 乃驛報太子，并賜諸臣書曰：「朕自將若此，云何？」

translations.literal: He then reported by relay to the crown prince, and also sent letters to his ministers saying: "I have led in person thus—what say you?
translations.idiomatic: He sent word by post relay to the crown prince and wrote his ministers: "I have led the army in person to this effect—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 因號所幸山爲駐蹕山，圖破陣狀，勒石紀功。

translations.literal: He therefore named the mountain where he had halted Mount Zhubi, drew the dispositions of the battle array, and carved stone to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He named the mountain where he had halted Mount Zhubi, had the battle array diagrammed, and had his victory cut into stone.

sentences.zh: 拜延壽鴻臚卿，惠真司農卿。

translations.literal: Yanshou was appointed Grand Master of the Palace; Huizhen was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanshou was made Grand Master of the Palace; Huizhen was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 候騎獲覘人，帝解其縛，自言不食且三日，命飼之，賜以屩，遣曰：「歸語莫離支，若須軍中進退，可遣人至吾所。」

translations.literal: Scout horsemen captured a spy. The emperor loosened his bonds; the man said he had not eaten for three days. He ordered him fed, gave him sandals, and sent him away saying: "Return and tell the Molizhi: if you need to know our army's movements, you may send someone to my camp.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts captured a spy. Taizong freed him; the man said he had gone without food for three days. Taizong had him fed, gave him sandals, and sent him off with this message: "Tell Gaisuwen: if he needs to know how our army will advance or withdraw, he may send a man to my headquarters."

sentences.zh: 帝每營不作塹壘，謹斥候而已，而士運糧，雖單騎，虜不敢鈔。

translations.literal: At each encampment the emperor did not build trenches and ramparts, only careful scouts; yet when soldiers transported grain, even a lone rider—the barbarians did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: At every camp Taizong built no trenches or ramparts, relying only on vigilant scouts—yet when his men hauled grain, even a lone rider went unmolested; the enemy did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 帝與勣議所攻，帝曰：「吾聞安市地險而衆悍，莫離支擊不能下，因與之。

translations.literal: The emperor and Li Shiji discussed which place to attack. The emperor said: "I have heard that Ansi's terrain is dangerous and its people fierce; the Molizhi struck but could not take it, and so left it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong and Li Shiji debated their next target. Taizong said, "I have heard that Ansi sits on hard ground and fields a stubborn garrison. Gaisuwen could not reduce it and left it standing.

sentences.zh: 建安恃險絕，粟多而士少，若出其不意攻之，不相救矣。

translations.literal: Jian'an relies on precipitous inaccessibility; it has much grain but few troops. If we strike it by surprise, they cannot rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an trusts its sheer cliffs, hoards grain, and keeps few men. A surprise stroke there would leave the garrisons unable to help each other.

sentences.zh: 建安得，則安市在吾腹中。」

translations.literal: Once Jian'an is taken, Ansi will be in our belly.
translations.idiomatic: Take Jian'an, and Ansi lies in the palm of our hand."

sentences.zh: 勣曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Li Shiji said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji said, "No.

sentences.zh: 積糧遼東，而西擊建安，賊將梗我歸路，不如先攻安市。」

translations.literal: With grain accumulated in Liaodong, if we march west to strike Jian'an, the enemy will block our route home. Better first attack Ansi."
translations.idiomatic: Our stores are piled in Liaodong. If we swing west against Jian'an, the enemy will cut our line of retreat. Better strike Ansi first."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Well argued."

sentences.zh: 遂攻之，未能下。

translations.literal: They then attacked it but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They laid siege to Ansi but could not bring it down.

sentences.zh: 延壽、惠真謀曰：「烏骨城傉薩已耄，朝攻而夕可下。

translations.literal: Yanshou and Huizhen plotted: "At Ugeo the lord is already old; attack in the morning and by evening it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanshou and Huizhen urged: "The lord of Ugeo is aged. Strike at dawn and the city will fall by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 烏骨拔，則平壤舉矣。」

translations.literal: If Ugeo is taken, Pyongyang will rise.
translations.idiomatic: Take Ugeo, and Pyongyang will follow."

sentences.zh: 群臣亦以張亮軍在沙城，召之一昔至，若取烏骨，度鴨淥，迫其腹心，計之善者。

translations.literal: The ministers also thought that Zhang Liang's army was at Shacheng, and if summoned could arrive in one night; if Ugeo were taken and they crossed the Yalu, pressing on the enemy's heart—that was the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court likewise argued that Zhang Liang's fleet lay at Shacheng and could reach them in a single night. Seize Ugeo, cross the Yalu, and drive into Goguryeo's vitals—the best plan of all.

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「天子行師不徼幸。

translations.literal: Wuji said: "When the Son of Heaven campaigns, he does not gamble on luck.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Wuji said, "When the Son of Heaven takes the field, he does not stake the realm on a gamble.

sentences.zh: 安市衆十萬在吾後，不如先破之，乃驅而南，萬全勢也。」

translations.literal: Ansi has a hundred thousand men in our rear. Better first break them, then drive south—an utterly secure position.
translations.idiomatic: Ansi still holds a hundred thousand men at our backs. Break that city first, then march south—that is the posture of perfect safety."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was therefore halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was set aside.

sentences.zh: 城中見帝旌麾，輒乘陴噪，帝怒。

translations.literal: When those in the city saw the emperor's standards and banners they would mount the parapet and shout; the emperor was angered.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the garrison caught sight of Taizong's banners they scrambled onto the battlements and jeered. Taizong was furious.

sentences.zh: 勣請破日男子盡誅。

translations.literal: Li Shiji asked that when the city was taken all males be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji asked leave to slaughter every male in the city once the walls fell.

sentences.zh: 虜聞，故死戰。

translations.literal: The barbarians heard this and therefore fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy heard of it and fought all the harder, resolved to die where they stood.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗築距闉攻東南，虜增陴以守。

translations.literal: Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, built a siege mound to attack the southeast; the barbarians raised the parapet to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, raised a siege mound against the southeast wall; the defenders heightened the parapet to meet him.

sentences.zh: 勣攻其西，撞車所壞，隨輒串柵爲樓。

translations.literal: Li Shiji attacked the west. Where battering carts broke through, they immediately linked palisades into towers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji assailed the west face. Where the rams breached the wall, his men at once lashed palisades into fighting towers.

sentences.zh: 帝聞城中雞彘聲，曰：「圍久，突無黔煙。

translations.literal: The emperor heard chicken and pig sounds in the city and said: "The siege has been long, yet suddenly no cooking smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard chickens and pigs within the walls and said, "We have besieged them for so long, yet suddenly there is no cook-fire smoke.

sentences.zh: 今雞彘鳴，必殺以饗士，虜且夜出。」

translations.literal: Now chickens and pigs cry—they must be slaughtered to feast the soldiers; the barbarians will sortie by night.
translations.idiomatic: Now the livestock cry out—they are butchering them to feed the garrison. The enemy will sally tonight."

sentences.zh: 詔嚴兵。

translations.literal: He ordered the army to stand ready.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the troops to stand to arms.

sentences.zh: 丙夜，虜數百人縋而下，悉禽之。

translations.literal: At the third watch, several hundred barbarians lowered themselves on ropes; all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the third watch of the night several hundred enemy soldiers slipped down on ropes; every one was taken.

sentences.zh: 道宗以樹枚裹土積之，距闉成，迫城不數丈，果毅都尉傅伏愛守之，自高而排其城，城且頹，伏愛私去所部，虜兵得自頹城出，據而塹斷之，積火縈盾固守。

translations.literal: Daozong wrapped earth in tree branches and piled it; the siege mound was completed within a few zhang of the wall. Valiant Cavalry Commander Fu A'ai held it. From above they undermined the wall; the wall was about to collapse. Fu A'ai privately left his post; enemy troops got out through the collapsing wall, seized the breach and cut trenches, piled fire and ringed shields to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong packed earth in wicker frames of branches and heaped it up until the mound stood only a few yards from the wall. Valiant Cavalry Commander Fu A'ai held the crest. From above his men undermined the masonry; the wall was giving way. Fu A'ai slipped away from his command without leave. The defenders poured through the breach, seized it, dug a cutting across the approach, and with heaped fire and shield walls made a stubborn stand.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，斬伏愛，敕諸將擊之，三日不克。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, beheaded Fu A'ai, and ordered the generals to attack; for three days they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was enraged, executed Fu A'ai, and ordered his generals to storm the breach. For three days they could not break through.

sentences.zh: 有詔班師，拔遼、蓋二州之人以歸。

translations.literal: There was an edict to withdraw the army; the people of Liao and Gaizhou prefectures were brought away.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the army to withdraw. The populations of Liao and Gaizhou were uprooted and marched home with the host.

sentences.zh: 兵過城下，城中屏息偃旗，酋長登城再拜，帝嘉其守，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: As the army passed below the city wall, those in the city held their breath and lowered their banners; the chieftain mounted the wall and bowed twice. The emperor praised their defense and gave them a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: As the columns filed past Ansi, the garrison held its breath and furled its banners. The city chief mounted the wall and bowed twice. Taizong praised their defense and granted a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遼州粟尚十萬斛，士取不能盡。

translations.literal: At Liaozhou there still remained a hundred thousand hu of grain; the soldiers could not take it all.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaozhou a hundred thousand hu of grain still lay in the granaries; the army could not carry it away.

sentences.zh: 帝至渤錯水，阻淖，八十里車騎不通。

translations.literal: The emperor reached the Bochuo River, blocked by marsh; for eighty li chariots and horses could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong came to the Bochuo River and found the way choked by bog. For eighty li neither cart nor horse could advance.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、楊師道等率萬人斬樵築道，聯車爲梁，帝負薪馬上助役。

translations.literal: Changsun Wuji, Yang Shidao and others led ten thousand men to cut wood and build a road, linking wagons as a bridge; the emperor carried firewood on horseback to help the work.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Wuji, Yang Shidao, and others led ten thousand men to fell timber and lay a causeway, chaining wagons into a bridge. Taizong loaded firewood onto his saddle and worked beside them.

sentences.zh: 十月，兵畢度，雪甚，詔屬燎以待濟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army finished crossing. Snow was heavy; an edict ordered fuel gathered to await the crossing.
