translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army finished the crossing. Snow fell thick; an edict ordered fuel stockpiled to see them through.

sentences.zh: 始行，士十萬，馬萬匹；

translations.literal: At the start they marched with a hundred thousand soldiers and ten thousand horses;
translations.idiomatic: When they set out there were a hundred thousand soldiers and ten thousand horses;

sentences.zh: 逮還，物故裁千余，馬死十八。

translations.literal: On returning, dead were only a little over a thousand; horses dead, eighteen [in ten].
translations.idiomatic: On the march home, dead among the men numbered barely a thousand; of the horses, eighteen in every hundred perished.

sentences.zh: 船師七萬，物故亦數百。

translations.literal: The fleet of seventy thousand—dead also several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang's fleet of seventy thousand sailors lost only a few hundred.

sentences.zh: 詔集戰骸葬柳城，祭乙太牢，帝臨哭，從臣皆流涕。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the battle dead gathered and buried at Liucheng, sacrifice with the great offering of the second rank; the emperor came to mourn, and attending ministers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gathered the fallen and buried them at Liucheng with the grandest rites. Taizong came in person to weep over them, and every minister in attendance wept with him.

sentences.zh: 帝總飛騎入臨渝關，皇太子迎道左。

translations.literal: The emperor led the Flying Cavalry into Linyu Pass; the crown prince met him on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong led the Flying Cavalry through Linyu Pass; the crown prince met him on the roadside.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與太子別，御褐袍，曰：「俟見爾乃更。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor parted from the crown prince, he wore a brown robe and said: "Wait until I see you before I change.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong had parted from the crown prince he wore a plain brown robe and said, "I will not change it until I see you again."

sentences.zh: 袍曆二時弗易，至穿穴。

translations.literal: For two seasons he did not change the robe, until it was worn through with holes.
translations.idiomatic: For two seasons he never changed it, until the cloth was threadbare and riddled with holes.

sentences.zh: 群臣請更服，帝曰：「士皆敝衣，吾可新服邪？」

translations.literal: The ministers asked that he change his garments; the emperor said: "The soldiers all wear worn-out clothing—how can I wear new robes?
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged him to change clothes. Taizong said, "My men march in rags—how can I dress in something new?"

sentences.zh: 及是，太子進潔衣，乃御。

translations.literal: When this moment came, the crown prince presented a clean robe, and only then did he put it on.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the crown prince bring him a fresh robe, and at last he consented to wear it.

sentences.zh: 遼降口萬四千，當沒爲奴婢，前集幽州，將分賞士。

translations.literal: Liaodong captives, fourteen thousand persons, were to be enslaved; they had earlier been assembled at Youzhou and were about to be distributed as rewards to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen thousand Liaodong captives were bound for slavery. They had already been gathered at Youzhou to be parceled out as booty among the troops.

sentences.zh: 帝以父子夫婦離析，詔有司以布帛贖之，原爲民，列拜歡舞，三日不息。

translations.literal: Because fathers and sons, husbands and wives had been torn apart, the emperor ordered the authorities to ransom them with cloth and silk and restore them as commoners; they knelt in ranks, bowing and dancing in joy, for three days without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Moved that families had been broken apart, Taizong ordered officials to ransom them with cloth and silk and restore them to free status. They knelt in ranks, bowing and dancing for three days without pause.

sentences.zh: 延壽既降，以憂死，獨惠真至長安。

translations.literal: After Yanshou had surrendered, he died of grief; only Huizhen reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou had surrendered, but grief killed him; only Huizhen ever reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 明年春，藏遣使者上方物，且謝罪；

translations.literal: The next spring, Zang sent envoys to present local products and also to express regret.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring King Zang sent envoys with tribute goods and an apology.

sentences.zh: 獻二姝口，帝敕還之，謂使者曰：「色者人所重，然湣其去親戚以傷乃心，我不取也。」

translations.literal: He offered two beautiful women; the emperor ordered them returned and told the envoys: "Beauty is what men prize, yet I pity that you left your kin and wounded your hearts—I will not take them.
translations.idiomatic: They presented two beautiful women. Taizong sent them back and told the envoys, "Men prize beauty, but I pity your leaving kin behind to break your hearts. I will not take them."

sentences.zh: 初，師還，帝以弓服賜蓋蘇文，受之，不遣使者謝，於是下詔削棄朝貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the army returned, the emperor had bestowed bow garments on Gaisuwen; he accepted them but sent no envoy to give thanks, whereupon an edict was issued cutting off and abandoning his tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the army withdrew, Taizong had sent Gaisuwen bow garments as a gift. Gaisuwen accepted them but never sent thanks. An edict then cut off his tribute missions entirely.

sentences.zh: 又明年三月，詔左武衛大將軍牛進達爲青丘道行軍大總管，右武衛將軍李海岸副之，自萊州度海；

translations.literal: Again the next year, in the third month, an edict appointed Left Martial Guard Grand General Niu Jinda Grand Marching Commander of the Qingqiu Route, with Right Martial Guard General Li Hai'an as deputy, to cross the sea from Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, in the third month, an edict named Niu Jinda, grand general of the Left Martial Guards, grand marching commander of the Qingqiu route, with Li Hai'an of the Right Martial Guards as his deputy, to cross the sea from Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 李勣爲遼東道行軍大總管，右武衛將軍孫貳朗、右屯衛大將軍鄭仁泰副之，率營州都督兵，繇新城道以進。

translations.literal: Li Shiji was made Grand Marching Commander of the Liaodong Route, with Right Martial Guard General Sun Erlang and Right Encampment Guard Grand General Zheng Rentai as deputies, leading the troops of the Yingzhou protector-general, advancing by the Xincheng road.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji was made grand marching commander of the Liaodong route, with Sun Erlang and Zheng Rentai as deputies, leading the Yingzhou protector-general's troops up the Xincheng road.

sentences.zh: 次南蘇、木底，虜兵戰不勝，焚其郛。

translations.literal: They halted at Nansu and Mudi; the barbarian troops fought but could not win and burned their outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: At Nansu and Mudi the enemy gave battle and lost, then burned their own outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 七月，進達等取石城，進攻積利城，斬級數千，乃皆還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Jinda and the others took Shicheng, attacked Jili City, beheaded several thousand, and then all returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jinda's force took Shicheng, assaulted Jili City, and slew several thousand before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 藏遣子莫離支高任武來朝，因謝罪。

translations.literal: Zang sent his son, Mo-li-zhi Gao Renwu, to court and thereby expressed regret.
translations.idiomatic: Zang sent his son Gao Renwu, who held the title Mo-li-zhi, to court with an apology.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔右武衛大將軍薛萬徹爲青丘道行軍大總管，右衛將軍裴行方副之，自海道入。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two, an edict appointed Right Martial Guard Grand General Xue Wanche Grand Marching Commander of the Qingqiu Route, with Right Guard General Pei Xingfang as deputy, to enter by the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year an edict made Xue Wanche grand marching commander of the Qingqiu route, with Pei Xingfang as deputy, to invade by sea.

sentences.zh: 部將古神感與虜戰曷山，虜潰；

translations.literal: Subordinate commander Gu Shengan fought the barbarians at Mount Ye, and the barbarians fled.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Gu Shengan fought the enemy at Mount Ye and routed them.

sentences.zh: 虜乘暝襲我舟，伏兵破之。

translations.literal: The barbarians took advantage of dusk to raid our ships; ambush troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck our fleet at dusk, but our ambushers broke the attack.

sentences.zh: 萬徹度鴨淥，次泊灼城，拒四十里而舍。

translations.literal: Wanche crossed the Yalu, halted at Bozhuo City, and encamped forty li from it.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche crossed the Yalu, camped at Bozhuo City, and pitched his tents forty li away.

sentences.zh: 虜懼，皆棄邑居去。

translations.literal: The barbarians were afraid and all abandoned their settlements and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the enemy abandoned every town and fled.

sentences.zh: 大酋所夫孫拒戰，萬徹擊斬之，遂圍城，破其援兵三萬，乃還。

translations.literal: A great chief, Suofusun, resisted in battle; Wanche struck and beheaded him, then besieged the city, destroyed their relief force of thirty thousand, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A great chief named Suofusun gave battle; Wanche slew him, besieged the city, shattered a relief army of thirty thousand, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝與長孫無忌計曰：「高麗困吾師之入，戶亡耗，田歲不收，蓋蘇文築城增陴，下饑臥死溝壑，不勝敝矣。

translations.literal: The emperor conferred with Zhangsun Wuji, saying: "Goguryeo is exhausted by our armies' incursions—the households are depleted, the fields yield nothing year after year; Gaisuwen builds walls and raises ramparts; below, the hungry lie dead in ditches and ravines—they cannot endure their ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told Zhangsun Wuji, "Goguryeo is worn down by our invasions. Households are emptying, harvests fail year after year. Gaisuwen piles stone on stone while his people starve and die in the ditches. They cannot hold out much longer.

sentences.zh: 明年以三十萬衆，公爲大總管，一舉可滅也。」

translations.literal: Next year with three hundred thousand men, you as grand commander—a single stroke can extinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, with three hundred thousand men under your command as grand marshal, we can destroy them in one blow."

sentences.zh: 乃詔劍南大治船，蜀人願輸財江南，計直作舟，舟取縑千二百。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered great shipbuilding in Jiannan; Shu people wished to contribute wealth to the Jiangnan, calculating value to build boats—each boat required twelve hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then launched a vast shipbuilding program in Jiannan. Shu families offered money to the Jiangnan yards, reckoned in silk—twelve hundred bolts of fine gauze per vessel.

sentences.zh: 巴、蜀大騷，邛、眉、雅三州獠皆反，發隴西、峽內兵二萬擊定之。

translations.literal: Ba and Shu were greatly agitated; the Liao of Qiong, Mei, and Ya prefectures all rebelled, and twenty thousand troops from Longxi and within the gorges were sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Shu erupted in unrest. The tribal peoples of Qiong, Mei, and Ya all rose in revolt, and twenty thousand troops from Longxi and the gorge country were sent to crush them.

sentences.zh: 始，帝決取虜，故詔陝州刺史孫伏伽、萊州刺史李道裕儲糧械於三山浦、烏胡島，越州都督治大艎偶舫以待。

translations.literal: At the outset the emperor had resolved to take the barbarians, and so had decreed Shanzhou Prefect Sun Fuga and Laizhou Prefect Li Daoyu to store grain and weapons at Sanshan Harbor and Wuhu Island, and the Yuezhou protector-general to build great paired warships in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Taizong had set his mind on conquest, ordering Sun Fuga of Shanzhou and Li Daoyu of Laizhou to stock grain and arms at Sanshan Harbor and Wuhu Island, while the Yuezhou protector-general built great paired warships to await the campaign.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，乃皆罷。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, it all was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, the whole enterprise was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 藏遣使者奉慰。

translations.literal: Zang sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Zang sent envoys to offer condolences on the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，藏以靺鞨兵攻契丹，戰新城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui, Zang attacked the Khitan with Mohe troops, fighting at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui, Zang struck the Khitan with Mohe auxiliaries at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 大風，矢皆還激，爲契丹所乘，大敗。

translations.literal: A great wind blew; arrows all flew back against them; the Khitan seized the chance and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind blew their arrows back into their own ranks. The Khitan seized the moment and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 契丹火野復戰，人死相藉，積屍而塚之。

translations.literal: The Khitan set the wilderness ablaze and fought again; the dead lay piled upon one another; corpses were heaped into burial mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan set the plain afire and fought again. The dead lay in heaps, and the living piled the corpses into burial mounds.

sentences.zh: 遣使者告捷，高宗爲露布於朝。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to report victory; Gaozong proclaimed a battlefield bulletin at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zang sent envoys claiming victory, and Gaozong proclaimed the triumph at court.

sentences.zh: 六年，新羅訴高麗、靺鞨奪三十六城，惟天子哀救。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Silla petitioned that Goguryeo and Mohe had seized thirty-six cities, begging only that the Son of Heaven pity and rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Silla appealed that Goguryeo and the Mohe had taken thirty-six of its cities, begging the Son of Heaven for pity and rescue.

sentences.zh: 有詔營州都督程名振、左衛中郎將蘇定方率師討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yingzhou Protector-general Cheng Mingzhen and Left Guard Mid-grade General Su Dingfang to lead troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Cheng Mingzhen, protector-general of Yingzhou, and Su Dingfang of the Left Guards to lead a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 至新城，敗高麗兵，火外郛及墟落，引還。

translations.literal: Reaching Xincheng, they defeated Goguryeo troops, burned the outer walls and ruined hamlets, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Xincheng, routed the Goguryeo army, burned the outer walls and outlying settlements, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，復遣名振率薛仁貴攻之，未能克。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, Mingzhen was again sent leading Xue Rengui to attack, but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing, Mingzhen was sent again with Xue Rengui to attack, but they could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 後二年，天子已平百濟，乃以左驍衛大將軍契苾力何、右武衛大將軍蘇定方、左驍衛將軍劉伯英率諸將出浿江、遼東、平壤道討之。

translations.literal: Two years later, the Son of Heaven having pacified Baekje, Qibi Heli, Grand General of the Left Swift Cavalry Guards, Su Dingfang, Grand General of the Right Martial Guards, and Liu Boying, General of the Left Swift Cavalry Guards, were appointed to lead the generals out by the Taedong, Liaodong, and Pyongyang routes to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, with Baekje already subdued, Qibi Heli, Su Dingfang, and Liu Boying were placed at the head of the generals advancing by the Taedong, Liaodong, and Pyongyang routes to strike Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，大募兵，拜置諸將，天子欲自行，蔚州刺史李君球建言：「高麗小丑，何至傾中國事之？

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo, troops were recruited on a grand scale and generals appointed and posted; the Son of Heaven wished to lead in person; Youzhou Prefect Li Junqiu remonstrated: "Goguryeo is a petty foe—why must the whole empire be turned to this affair?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longshuo the court raised a vast army and posted its generals. The emperor meant to lead in person, but Youzhou prefect Li Junqiu objected: "Goguryeo is a trifling enemy—why turn the whole empire upside down for it?

sentences.zh: 有如高麗既滅，必發兵以守，少發則威不振，多發人不安，是天下疲於轉戍。

translations.literal: If Goguryeo should be destroyed, troops must be sent to garrison it—send too few and authority will not awe; send too many and the people will be unsettled—the realm will wear itself out on rotating frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Goguryeo fell, we would have to garrison it. Too few troops and our authority would not hold; too many and the people would grow restless. The empire would exhaust itself shuttling men to distant posts.

sentences.zh: 臣謂征之未如勿征，滅之未如勿滅。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that not campaigning is better than campaigning, and not destroying them is better than destroying them.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant would say: better not to campaign than to campaign, and better not to destroy them than to destroy them."

sentences.zh: 亦會武后苦邀，帝乃止。

translations.literal: At the same time Empress Wu pressed him relentlessly, and the emperor ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Empress Wu pressed him hard to go, but in the end the emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 八月，定方破虜兵于浿江，奪馬邑山，遂圍平壤。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Dingfang defeated the barbarian troops on the Taedong, seized Mayi Mountain, and thereupon besieged Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Su Dingfang shattered the enemy on the Taedong, took Mayi Mountain, and laid siege to Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，龐孝泰以嶺南兵壁蛇水，蓋蘇文攻之，舉軍沒；

translations.literal: The next year, Pang Xiaotai stationed Lingnan troops at Serpent Water; Gaisuwen attacked them and the whole army perished.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Pang Xiaotai encamped Lingnan troops at Serpent Water. Gaisuwen attacked, and the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 定方解而歸。

translations.literal: Dingfang lifted the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang raised the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，藏遣子男福從天子封泰山，還而蓋蘇文死，子男生代爲莫離支，有弟男建、男產相怨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, Zang sent his son Nam-bok to accompany the Son of Heaven in the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai; on their return Gaisuwen died; his son Nam-geon succeeded as Mo-li-zhi; he had younger brothers Nam-jian and Nam-san, who bore mutual hatred.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianfeng, Zang sent his son Nam-bok to attend the emperor's Fengshan rites at Mount Tai. On their return Gaisuwen was dead. His son Nam-geon had become Mo-li-zhi, while his brothers Nam-jian and Nam-san nursed a bitter feud.

sentences.zh: 男生據國內城，遣子獻誠入朝求救，蓋蘇文弟淨土亦請割地降。

translations.literal: Nam-geon held the inner capital; he sent his son Hyeoncheong to court to beg rescue; Gaisuwen's younger brother Jingtu also asked to cede territory and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Nam-geon held the inner capital and sent his son Hyeoncheong to court pleading for aid. Gaisuwen's brother Jingtu also offered to surrender territory.

sentences.zh: 乃詔契苾何力爲遼東道安撫大使，左金吾衛將軍龐同善、營州都督高偘爲行軍總管，左武衛將軍薛仁貴、左監門將軍李謹行殿而行。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Qibi Heli Liaodong Route Pacification Commissioner, Left Golden Crow Guard General Pang Tongshan and Yingzhou Protector-general Gao Kan as marching commanders, and Left Martial Guard General Xue Rengui and Left Palace Gate Guard General Li Jinxing to march as the rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Qibi Heli pacification commissioner of the Liaodong route, with Pang Tongshan and Gao Kan as marching commanders and Xue Rengui and Li Jinxing bringing up the rear.

sentences.zh: 九月，同善破高麗兵，男生率師來會。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Tongshan defeated Goguryeo troops; Nam-geon led his army to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Tongshan routed the Goguryeo army, and Nam-geon marched up with his own forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 詔拜男生特進、遼東大都督兼平壤道安撫大使，封玄菟郡公。

translations.literal: An edict invested Nam-geon as specially advanced, Grand Protector-general of Liaodong and concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the Pyongyang Route, enfeoffing him as Duke of Xuantu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Nam-geon was appointed specially advanced, grand protector-general of Liaodong and pacification commissioner of the Pyongyang route, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 又以李勣爲遼東道行軍大總管兼安撫大使，與契苾何力、龐同善并力。

translations.literal: Li Shiji was again appointed Grand Marching Commander of the Liaodong Route and concurrently Pacification Commissioner, joining forces with Qibi Heli and Pang Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji was again made grand marching commander and pacification commissioner of the Liaodong route, to unite his strength with Qibi Heli and Pang Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 詔獨孤卿云由鴨淥道，郭待封積利道，劉仁願畢列道，金待問海穀道，並爲行軍總管，受勣節度；

translations.literal: An edict named Dugu Qingyun by the Yalu Route, Guo Daifeng by the Jili Route, Liu Renyuan by the Bilie Route, and Jin Daiwen by the Haigu Route—all as marching commanders, subject to Shiji's command.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Qingyun was ordered up the Yalu route, Guo Daifeng along the Jili route, Liu Renyuan along the Bilie route, and Jin Daiwen along the Haigu route—all as marching commanders under Li Shiji's authority.

sentences.zh: 轉燕、趙食廥遼東。

translations.literal: Grain depots of Yan and Zhao were shifted to supply Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries throughout Yan and Zhao were tapped to feed the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，勣引道次新城，合諸將謀曰：「新城，賊西鄙，不先圖，餘城未易下。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Shiji led the army and halted at Xincheng; he gathered the generals to counsel, saying: "Xincheng is the enemy's western frontier. If we do not take it first, the remaining cities will not be easy to reduce.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Li Shiji led the army to a halt at Xincheng. He called his generals together and said, "Xincheng is the enemy's western gate. Unless we seize it first, the rest of their cities will not fall easily."

sentences.zh: 遂壁西南山臨城，城人縛戍酋出降。

translations.literal: Thereupon they walled on the southwest mountain overlooking the city; the townspeople bound the garrison chief and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They entrenched on the mountain southwest of the city and pressed the walls from above. The townspeople bound their garrison chief and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 勣進拔城十有六。

translations.literal: Shiji advanced and captured sixteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji pushed forward and took sixteen cities.

sentences.zh: 郭待封以舟師濟海，趨平壤。

translations.literal: Guo Daifeng with the fleet crossed the sea, pressing toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Daifeng put his fleet to sea and bore down on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，勣率仁貴拔扶餘城，它城三十皆納款。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Shiji led Rengui to take Fuyu city; thirty other cities all tendered submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Shiji and Xue Rengui stormed Fuyu. Thirty other towns submitted without a fight.

sentences.zh: 同善、偘守新城，男建遣兵襲之，仁貴救偘，戰金山，不勝。

translations.literal: Tongshan and Kan guarded Xincheng; Nam-jian sent troops to attack them; Rengui rescued Kan and fought at Jin Mountain without victory.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tongshan and Gao Kan held Xincheng. Nam-jian sent troops against them, and Rengui marched to Kan's relief. They fought at Jin Mountain and were driven back.

sentences.zh: 高麗鼓而進，銳甚。

translations.literal: Goguryeo beat drums and advanced, very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo army came on to the beat of drums, fierce and pressing.

sentences.zh: 仁貴橫擊，大破之，斬首五萬級，拔南蘇、木底、蒼岩三城，引兵略地，與勣會。

translations.literal: Rengui struck across their line, thoroughly defeated them, cut heads to fifty thousand, took the three cities of Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan, led troops to raid territory, and joined Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui hit them on the flank and broke them utterly. Fifty thousand heads were taken, and the cities of Nansu, Mudi, and Cangyan fell. He swept the countryside with his columns and rejoined Shiji.

sentences.zh: 侍御史賈言忠計事還，帝問軍中云何。

translations.literal: Attending censor Jia Yanzhong returned from surveying affairs; the emperor asked how things stood in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The attending censor Jia Yanzhong came back from inspecting the campaign. The emperor asked him how the army fared.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「必克。

translations.literal: He replied: "We will surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 昔先帝問罪，所以不得志者，虜未有邅也。

translations.literal: Formerly when the late emperor demanded satisfaction, the reason he did not achieve his aim was that the barbarians had not yet met with misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor carried the war to them, he failed to finish the work only because fortune had not yet turned against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：'軍無媒，中道回'。

translations.literal: As the proverb says: 'An army without a guide turns back midway.'
translations.idiomatic: There is a saying: 'An army without a guide turns home halfway.'

sentences.zh: 今男生兄弟鬩很，爲我鄉導，虜之情偽，我盡知之，將忠士力，臣故曰必克。

translations.literal: Now Nam-geon and his brothers are at bitter feud and serve as our path-guides; the barbarians' truth and deceit—we know them all; I will marshal loyal soldiers' strength—thus your subject says we will surely conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Now Nam-geon and his brothers are tearing one another apart and act as our guides in their own land. We know every ruse the enemy can play. Give me loyal men and I will bring their strength to bear—that is why I say victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 且高麗祕記曰：'不及九百年，當有八十大將滅之。

translations.literal: Moreover Goguryeo's secret chronicle says: 'Before nine hundred years are out, an eighty-year-old general will destroy it.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Goguryeo keeps a secret chronicle that says, 'Before nine hundred years have passed, a general of eighty will destroy the kingdom.'

sentences.zh: '高氏自漢有國，今九百年，勣年八十矣。

translations.literal: The Gao clan has had a state since Han; now it is nine hundred years, and Shiji is eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao have ruled since Han times—nine hundred years by now—and Shiji is eighty.

sentences.zh: 虜仍薦饑，人相掠賣，地震裂，狼狐入城，蚡穴于門，人心危駭，是行不再舉矣。」

translations.literal: The barbarians still suffer repeated famine; people rob and sell one another; the earth splits in quakes; wolves and foxes enter the city; mole crickets burrow at the gates; hearts are terror-stricken—this campaign will not be mounted again."
translations.idiomatic: Famine still stalks them year after year. Men rob and sell one another. The earth splits in earthquakes. Wolves and foxes wander the streets, and mole crickets burrow at the gates. Their people are sick with fear. They will not survive another campaign like this one."

sentences.zh: 男建以兵五萬襲扶餘，勣破之薩賀水上，斬首五千級，俘口三萬，器械牛馬稱之。

translations.literal: Nam-jian with fifty thousand troops raided Fuyu; Shiji defeated them on the Saha River, cut five thousand heads, took thirty thousand captives, and weapons, cattle, and horses in matching abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Nam-jian struck Fuyu with fifty thousand men. Shiji shattered them on the Saha River, took five thousand heads and thirty thousand prisoners, and seized arms, cattle, and horses beyond count.

sentences.zh: 進拔大行城。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Daxing city.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on and captured Daxing.

sentences.zh: 劉仁願與勣會，後期，召還當誅，赦流姚州。

translations.literal: Liu Renyuan joined Shiji but was late; summoned back and due for execution, he was pardoned and exiled to Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renyuan linked up with Shiji but arrived late. Recalled to face execution, he was spared and banished to Yaozhou instead.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力會勣軍於鴨淥，拔辱夷城，悉師圍平壤。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli joined Shiji's army at the Yalu, took Ruyi city, and drew up the full host to besiege Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli met Shiji on the Yalu, stormed Ruyi, and marched every man he had to the siege of Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，藏遣男產率首領百人樹素幡降，且請入朝，勣以禮見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zang sent Nam-san leading a hundred chieftains to raise white banners and surrender, also asking to enter court; Shiji received them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zang sent Nam-san with a hundred chieftains to raise white banners of surrender and beg leave to come to court. Shiji received them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 而男建猶固守，出戰數北。

translations.literal: Yet Nam-jian still held firm; he went out to battle several times and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Nam-jian still held the city, but each time he sallied forth he was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 大將浮屠信誠遣諜約內應。

translations.literal: Grand general Fotuo Xincheng sent spies to arrange an inner response.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general Fotuo Xincheng sent agents to arrange a rising within the walls.

sentences.zh: 五日，闔啟，兵噪而入，火其門，鬱焰四興，男建窘急，自刺不殊。

translations.literal: On the fifth day the gates were thrown wide; troops clamored in, fired the gates, dense flames rose on four sides; Nam-jian, in dire straits, stabbed himself but was not killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day the gates swung open. Soldiers poured in with a roar, torched the gate towers, and flames leaped up on every side. Nam-jian, cornered, stabbed himself but survived.

sentences.zh: 執藏、男建等，收凡五部百七十六城，戶六十九萬。

translations.literal: They seized Zang, Nam-jian, and the rest; in all they collected five departments, one hundred seventy-six cities, and six hundred ninety thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Zang, Nam-jian, and the rest were taken prisoner. Five departments, one hundred seventy-six cities, and six hundred ninety thousand households fell to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 詔勣便道獻俘昭陵，凱而還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shiji by the express route to present captives at Zhaoling and return in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was ordered to hurry home by the fastest road, present the captives at Taizong's tomb, and return in triumph.

sentences.zh: 十二月，帝坐含元殿，引見勣等，數俘於廷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the emperor sat in Hanyuan Hall, led in Shiji and the others, and enumerated the captives in court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor took his seat in Hanyuan Hall, received Shiji and his officers, and had the captives paraded and counted before the court.

sentences.zh: 以藏素脅制，赦爲司平太常伯，男產司宰少卿；

translations.literal: Because Zang had always been under coercion, he was pardoned and made Director of Ceremonial Ping; Nam-san was made Junior Director of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zang, who had long been a puppet king, was spared and named Director of Ceremonial Ping; Nam-san was made Junior Director of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 投男建黔州，百濟王扶餘隆嶺外；

translations.literal: Nam-jian was cast into Qianzhou; the king of Baekje, Fuyu Long, beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Nam-jian was banished to Qianzhou; the king of Baekje, Fuyu Long, was sent beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 以獻誠爲司衛卿，信誠爲銀青光祿大夫，男生右衛大將軍，何力行左衛大將軍，勣兼太子太師，仁貴威衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Hyeoncheong was made Director of the Guard; Xincheng Grand Master of Brilliant Glory with Silver Seal; Nam-geon Right Guard General; Heli Left Guard General; Shiji concurrent Crown Prince Preceptor; Rengui Majestic Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Hyeoncheong was made Director of the Guard, Xincheng Grand Master of Brilliant Glory with Silver Seal, Nam-geon general of the Right Guard, Heli general of the Left Guard, Shiji concurrent preceptor of the crown prince, and Rengui general of the Majestic Guard.

sentences.zh: 剖其地爲都督府者九，州四十二，縣百。

translations.literal: Their territory was carved into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and one hundred counties.
translations.idiomatic: Their land was carved into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and a hundred counties.

sentences.zh: 復置安東都護府，擢酋豪有功者授都督、刺史、令，與華官參治。

translations.literal: The Andong Protectorate was restored; meritorious tribal chiefs were promoted and given posts as protectors, prefects, and magistrates, to govern jointly with Chinese officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Andong Protectorate was re-established. Tribal leaders who had earned merit were made protectors, prefects, and magistrates to govern beside Chinese appointees.

sentences.zh: 仁貴爲都護，總兵鎮之。

translations.literal: Rengui was made protector and commanded troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was named protector and left at the head of an army to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 是歲郊祭，以高麗平，謝成於天。

translations.literal: That year at the border sacrifice, because Goguryeo was pacified, thanks were given to Heaven for the accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: That year, at the border sacrifice, the emperor gave thanks to Heaven for the fall of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 總章二年，徙高麗民三萬于江淮、山南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang, thirty thousand Goguryeo people were moved to the Jianghuai and Shannan regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zongzhang thirty thousand Goguryeo subjects were resettled in the Jianghuai and Shannan regions.

sentences.zh: 大長鉗牟岑率衆反，立藏外孫安舜爲主。

translations.literal: Senior chief Gwonmojin led the masses in revolt and set up Zang's grandson An-sun as lord.
translations.idiomatic: The senior chief Gwonmojin rose in rebellion and set Zang's grandson An-sun on the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔高偘東州道，李謹行燕山道，並爲行軍總管討之，遣司平太常伯楊昉綏納亡餘。

translations.literal: An edict named Gao Kan on the Eastern Route and Li Jinxing on the Yanshan Route—both as marching commanders to subdue them—and sent Director of Ceremonial Ping Yang Fang to pacify and accept the remnants.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kan was ordered up the Eastern route and Li Jinxing up the Yanshan route, each as marching commander to crush the revolt. Yang Fang, Director of Ceremonial Ping, was sent to win over those still at large.

sentences.zh: 舜殺鉗牟岑走新羅。

translations.literal: An-sun killed Gwonmojin and fled to Silla.
translations.idiomatic: An-sun killed Gwonmojin and fled to Silla.

sentences.zh: 偘徙都護府治遼東州，破叛兵于安市，又敗之泉山，俘新羅援兵二千。

translations.literal: Kan moved the protectorate seat to Liaodong prefecture, broke the rebels at An city, defeated them again at Quanshan, and captured two thousand Silla relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kan moved the protectorate seat to Liaodong prefecture, routed the rebels at An, beat them again at Quanshan, and took two thousand Silla auxiliaries prisoner.

sentences.zh: 李謹行破之於發廬河，再戰，俘馘萬計。

translations.literal: Li Jinxing defeated them on the Balu River; fighting twice more, captives and heads were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinxing broke them on the Balu River. After two more battles the prisoners and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是平壤痍殘不能軍，相率奔新羅，凡四年乃平。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pyongyang, crippled and unable to soldier, each led the other to flee to Silla; in all it took four years to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Pyongyang was too shattered to field an army. Survivors fled in waves to Silla. Four years passed before the land was truly quiet.

sentences.zh: 始，謹行留妻劉守伐奴城，虜攻之，劉擐甲勒兵守，賊引去。

translations.literal: At the outset, Jinxing left his wife Liu to guard Funu city; the barbarians attacked; Liu donned armor and rallied troops to defend; the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jinxing marched out, he had left his wife Liu to hold Funu. The enemy attacked, but Liu buckled on armor, mustered the garrison, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，封燕郡夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor commended her and enfeoffed her as Lady of Yen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her and enfeoffed her as Lady of Yen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，授藏遼東都督，封朝鮮郡王，還遼東以安餘民，先編僑內州者皆原遣，徙安東都護府於新城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, Zang was invested Liaodong Protector and enfeoffed King of Korean Commandery; he returned to Liaodong to settle the remaining people; those earlier registered in inner prefectures were all pardoned and sent back; the Andong Protectorate was moved to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yifeng, Zang was made protector of Liaodong and enfeoffed as King of Korean Commandery. He went back to settle the people who remained. Those earlier registered in interior prefectures were pardoned and sent home, and the Andong Protectorate was moved to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 藏與靺鞨謀反，未及發，召還放邛州，廝其人于河南、隴右，弱窶者留安東。

translations.literal: Zang plotted rebellion with the Mohe; before it broke out he was summoned back and released to Qiongzhou; his people were dispersed between Henan and Longyou; the weak and impoverished were left in Andong.
translations.idiomatic: Zang conspired with the Mohe to rebel, but word reached the court before the plot could fire. He was recalled and exiled to Qiongzhou. His followers were scattered across Henan and Longyou; only the weak and destitute were left in Andong.

sentences.zh: 藏以永淳初死，贈衛尉卿，葬頡利墓左，樹碑其阡。

translations.literal: Zang died in early Yongchun; he was posthumously made Grand Minister of the Guard, buried to the left of Jieli's tomb, with a monument at the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Zang died early in the Yongchun era. He was posthumously made Grand Minister of the Guard and buried to the left of Jieli's tomb, with a stele raised at the roadside.

sentences.zh: 舊城往往入新羅，遺人散奔突厥、靺鞨，由是高氏君長皆絕。

translations.literal: Old cities often passed into Silla; survivors scattered, fleeing to the Türks and Mohe; thereby the Gao clan chieftains all perished.
translations.idiomatic: One old stronghold after another fell to Silla. Survivors drifted toward the Türks and the Mohe. The line of Gao chieftains came to an end.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，以藏孫寶元爲朝鮮郡王。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era, Zang's grandson Bao-yuan was made King of Korean Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era Zang's grandson Bao-yuan was named King of Korean Commandery.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，進左鷹揚衛大將軍，更封忠誠國王，使統安東舊部，不行。

translations.literal: In early Shenli he was advanced to Left Hawkish Yang Guard General, further enfeoffed King of the State of Loyalty and Sincerity, and ordered to command the old Andong forces—not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenli era he was promoted to general of the Left Hawkish Yang Guard, re-enfeoffed as King of the State of Loyalty and Sincerity, and ordered to take command of the old Andong forces. The order was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 明年，以藏子德武爲安東都督，後稍自國。

translations.literal: The next year, Zang's son Deok-mu was made Andong Protector; later they gradually re-established their state.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zang's son Deok-mu was named protector of Andong. In time the Gao would rebuild something like a kingdom of their own.

sentences.zh: 至元和末，遣使者獻樂工云。

translations.literal: By the end of the Yuanhe era, they dispatched envoys presenting musicians.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Yuanhe reign they sent envoys bearing musicians as tribute.

sentences.zh: 百濟，扶餘別種也。

translations.literal: Baekje is a separate branch of the Fuyu people.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje was a collateral line of the Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 直京師東六千里而贏，濱海之陽，西界越州，南倭，北高麗，皆逾海乃至，其東，新羅也。

translations.literal: Due east of the capital six thousand li and more, on the sunny shore of the sea; west it borders Yue Prefecture; south Wa; north Goguryeo—all reachable only by crossing the sea; to the east, Silla.
translations.idiomatic: It lay more than six thousand li due east of the capital, on the sunward coast. Yue Prefecture marked its western marches; Wa lay to the south and Goguryeo to the north, each reachable only by sea. Silla stood to the east.

sentences.zh: 王居東、西二城，官有內臣佐平者宣納號令，內頭佐平主帑聚，內法佐平主禮，衛士佐平典衛兵，朝廷佐平主獄，兵官佐平掌外兵。

translations.literal: The king dwelt in eastern and western cities. Among officials, the Inner Minister Jwapyeong proclaimed and received orders; the Head Treasury Jwapyeong oversaw stores; the Inner Rites Jwapyeong oversaw ceremony; the Guard Jwapyeong commanded palace guards; the Court Jwapyeong oversaw prisons; the Military Jwapyeong commanded external troops.
translations.idiomatic: The king kept court in two cities, east and west. The Inner Minister Jwapyeong issued and received orders. The Head Treasury Jwapyeong held the granaries and treasury; the Inner Rites Jwapyeong presided over ritual; the Guard Jwapyeong commanded the palace guard; the Court Jwapyeong ran the prisons; the Military Jwapyeong led the field armies.

sentences.zh: 有六方，方統十郡。

translations.literal: There were six regions; each region commanded ten commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was divided into six regions, each governing ten commanderies.

sentences.zh: 大姓有八：沙氏，燕氏，軬氏，解氏，貞氏，國氏，木氏，䒤氏。

translations.literal: Great clans numbered eight: the Sha, Yeon, Pan, Hae, Jeon, Guk, Mok, and Ruo clans.
translations.idiomatic: Eight great clans held sway: Sha, Yeon, Pan, Hae, Jeon, Guk, Mok, and Ruo.

sentences.zh: 其法：反逆者誅，籍其家；

translations.literal: Their law: rebels were executed and their households registered for confiscation;
translations.idiomatic: By their law, treason was punished with death and the offender's household was seized;

sentences.zh: 殺人者，輸奴婢三贖罪；

translations.literal: murderers submitted three bond-servants to atone for the crime;
translations.idiomatic: murder was atoned by surrendering three bond-servants;

sentences.zh: 吏受賕及盜，三倍償，錮終身。

translations.literal: officials who took bribes or stole made threefold restitution and were imprisoned for life.
translations.idiomatic: officials who took bribes or stole had to repay threefold and were imprisoned for life.

sentences.zh: 俗與高麗同。

translations.literal: Customs were the same as Goguryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs matched those of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 有三島，生黃漆，六月刺取沈，色若金。

translations.literal: Three islands produced yellow lacquer; in the sixth month they pierced the trees, collected the sap, and sank it—its color like gold.
translations.idiomatic: Three islands yielded a yellow lacquer. In the sixth month they tapped the trees, collected the sap, and steeped it until the color shone like gold.

sentences.zh: 王服大袖紫袍，青錦褲，素皮帶，烏革履，烏羅冠飾以金花。

translations.literal: The king wore a large-sleeved purple robe, blue brocade trousers, a plain leather belt, black leather shoes, and a black gauze cap adorned with gold flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a purple robe with wide sleeves, blue brocade trousers, a plain leather belt, black leather shoes, and a black gauze cap set with gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 群臣絳衣，飾冠以銀花。

translations.literal: Ministers wore crimson garments; their caps were adorned with silver flowers.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers dressed in crimson and wore caps worked with silver flowers.

sentences.zh: 禁民衣絳紫。

translations.literal: Commoners were forbidden to wear crimson and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were forbidden crimson and purple.

sentences.zh: 有文籍，紀時月如華人。

translations.literal: They had written records and reckoned months and seasons as the Chinese do.
translations.idiomatic: They kept written records and reckoned the calendar much as the Chinese did.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，王扶餘璋始遣使獻果下馬，自是數朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, King Fuyu Jang first sent envoys presenting fruits and horses; from then on tribute missions were frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, King Fuyu Jang sent his first embassy with fruit and horses. Thereafter his envoys came often.

sentences.zh: 高祖冊爲帶方郡王、百濟王。

translations.literal: Gaozu enfeoffed him King of Daifang Commandery and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu invested him as King of Daifang Commandery and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 後五年，獻明光鎧，且訟高麗梗貢道。

translations.literal: Five years later he presented bright armor and also complained that Goguryeo blocked the tribute route.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he sent suits of bright armor and pleaded that Goguryeo was choking the tribute road.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀初，詔使者平其怨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's Zhenguan reign, an edict ordered an envoy to settle their grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizong's Zhenguan reign the throne sent an envoy to settle the quarrel.

sentences.zh: 又與新羅世仇，數相侵，帝賜璽書曰：「新羅，朕蕃臣，王之鄰國。

translations.literal: They were also hereditary enemies of Silla and repeatedly raided one another; the emperor bestowed an imperial letter saying: "Silla is My frontier subject and the King's neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje and Silla were hereditary foes and raided each other again and again. The emperor sent a sealed letter: "Silla is My frontier subject and your neighbor.

sentences.zh: 聞數相侵暴，朕已詔高麗、新羅申和，王宜忘前怨，識朕本懷。」

translations.literal: Hearing that you repeatedly invade and ravage one another, I have already ordered Goguryeo and Silla to restore harmony; the King should forget past resentments and grasp My true intent.
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have been harrying one another without cease. I have already commanded Goguryeo and Silla to make peace. Forget old injuries and read My true intent."

sentences.zh: 璋奉表謝，然兵亦不止。

translations.literal: Jang submitted a memorial of thanks, yet warfare still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jang answered with a memorial of thanks, but the raids did not stop.

sentences.zh: 再遣使朝，上鐵甲雕斧，帝優勞之，賜帛段三千。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys to court, presenting iron armor and carved axes; the emperor graciously comforted them and bestowed three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another embassy with iron armor and carved battle-axes. The emperor received them warmly and granted three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十五年，璋死，使者素服奉表曰：「君外臣百濟王扶餘璋卒。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Jang died; envoys in white mourning presented a memorial saying: "Your outer subject, the King of Baekje Fuyu Jang, has died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Jang died. Envoys in white mourning reported, "Your outer subject, the King of Baekje Fuyu Jang, is dead."

sentences.zh: 帝爲舉哀玄武門，贈光祿大夫，賻賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor held mourning at the Xuanwu Gate, posthumously granted him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and gave very generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at the Xuanwu Gate, posthumously named him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and sent lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 命祠部郎中鄭文表冊其子義慈爲柱國，紹王。

translations.literal: He ordered Court of Sacrifices Director Zheng Wenbiao to invest his son Uija as Pillar of State and succeed to the kingship.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zheng Wenbiao of the Court of Sacrifices to invest Jang's son Uija as Pillar of State and king in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 義慈事親孝，與兄弟友，時號「海東曾子」。

translations.literal: Uija served his parents filially and was friendly with his brothers; contemporaries styled him "Zengzi of the Eastern Sea."
translations.idiomatic: Uija was filial toward his parents and cordial with his brothers. Men of the time called him "Zengzi of the Eastern Sea."

sentences.zh: 明年，與高麗連和伐新羅，取四十餘城，發兵守之。

translations.literal: The next year he allied with Goguryeo to attack Silla, took more than forty cities, and deployed troops to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined Goguryeo against Silla, seized more than forty towns, and garrisoned them.

sentences.zh: 又謀取棠項城，絕貢道。

translations.literal: He also plotted to take Tangxiang city and cut off the tribute route.
translations.idiomatic: He also aimed to take Tangxiang and sever the road by which Silla sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 新羅告急，帝遣司農丞相裏玄獎齎詔書諭解。

translations.literal: Silla reported in emergency; the emperor sent Court of Imperial Granaries Director Xiangli Xuanjiang bearing an edict to counsel disengagement.
translations.idiomatic: Silla cried for help. The emperor sent Xiangli Xuanjiang of the Court of Imperial Granaries with an edict commanding both sides to stand down.

sentences.zh: 聞帝新討高麗，乃間取新羅七城；

translations.literal: Hearing that the emperor had newly campaigned against Goguryeo, he then opportunistically took seven Silla cities;
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the throne was newly at war with Goguryeo, he snatched seven Silla towns on the sly;

sentences.zh: 久之，又奪十餘城，因不朝貢。

translations.literal: after a long while he seized more than ten cities again and consequently ceased tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: and after a time seized more than ten more. He stopped sending tribute altogether.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，乃遣使者來，帝詔義慈曰：「海東三國，開基舊矣，地固犬牙。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended, he then sent envoys; the emperor addressed Uija: "The three kingdoms of the Eastern Sea have ancient foundations; their territories naturally interlock like dog's teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, Uija sent envoys again. The emperor wrote to him: "The three kingdoms of the Eastern Sea are old realms whose lands fit together like a dog's teeth.

sentences.zh: 比者隙爭侵校無寧歲，新羅高城重鎮皆爲王并，歸窮于朕，丐王歸地。

translations.literal: Recently, quarrels and invasions with reprisals—no peaceful year; Silla's Gao Castle and key fortresses have all been absorbed by the King; driven to extremity they appeal to Me; I beg the King to return their lands.
translations.idiomatic: Lately your feuds and raids have left no year at peace. You have swallowed Silla's Gao Castle and its great strongholds until they have nowhere left to turn but to Me. I ask you to give their lands back.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓一諸侯，尚存亡國，況朕萬方主，可不恤其危邪？

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi, though only one feudal lord, still preserved extinguished states—how much more I, lord of ten thousand realms—can I not pity their peril?
translations.idiomatic: Even Duke Huan of Qi, no more than one feudal lord among many, still restored fallen kingdoms. How can I, lord of all beneath heaven, turn away from their distress?

sentences.zh: 王所兼城宜還之，新羅所俘亦畀還王。

translations.literal: Cities the King has annexed ought to be returned; captives Silla holds should also be given back to the King.
translations.idiomatic: Return the cities you have taken. Silla must hand back the captives it holds from you as well.

sentences.zh: 不如詔者，任王決戰，朕將發契丹諸國，度遼深入。

translations.literal: If not as the edict commands, leave it to the King to decide battle; I will mobilize Khitan and other peoples, cross the Liao, and drive deep.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, choose your battle. I will raise the Khitan and the other northern peoples, cross the Liao, and march deep into your country.

sentences.zh: 王可思之，無後悔！」

translations.literal: The King may consider well—let him have no regrets!"
translations.idiomatic: Think on this, and do not rue it later!"

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，新羅訴百濟、高麗、靺鞨取北境三十城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui, Silla complained that Baekje, Goguryeo, and the Mohe had taken thirty cities on the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yonghui Silla reported that Baekje, Goguryeo, and the Mohe had seized thirty northern towns.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，乃詔左衛大將軍蘇定方爲神丘道行軍大總管，率左衛將軍劉伯英、右武衛將軍馮士貴、左驍衛將軍龐孝泰發新羅兵討之，自城山濟海。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, an edict then appointed Left Guard General Su Dingfang Grand General of the March on the Spirit-Mound Route, leading Left Guard General Liu Boying, Right Martial Guard General Feng Shigui, and Left Valiant Cavalry General Pang Xiaotai to launch Silla troops against them, crossing the sea from Chengshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianqing the throne named Su Dingfang, general of the Left Guard, Grand Marshal of the Spirit-Mound campaign. With Liu Boying, Feng Shigui, and Pang Xiaotai he led Silla levies against Baekje and put to sea from Chengshan.

sentences.zh: 百濟守熊津口，定方縱擊，虜大敗。

translations.literal: Baekje guarded the mouth of Ungjin; Dingfang loosed an attack and the enemy was thoroughly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje held the mouth of the Ungjin River. Dingfang struck and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 王師乘潮帆以進，趨真都城一舍止。

translations.literal: The imperial army rode the tide and sails to advance, pressing toward the capital of Sabi and halting one stage short.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial fleet rode tide and wind toward Sabi and halted one day's march from the capital.

sentences.zh: 虜悉衆拒，復破之，斬首萬餘級，拔其城。

translations.literal: The enemy rallied all their forces to resist; they were again defeated, heads cut to more than ten thousand, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy massed every man to resist and was broken again. More than ten thousand heads were taken and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 義慈挾太子隆走北鄙，定方圍之。

translations.literal: Uija took Crown Prince Yong and fled to the northern marches; Dingfang besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Uija fled north with Crown Prince Yong. Dingfang closed round them.

sentences.zh: 次子泰自立爲王，率衆固守，義慈孫文思曰：「王、太子固在，叔乃自王，若唐兵解去，如我父子何？」

translations.literal: The second son Tae declared himself king, led the multitude to hold fast, and Uija's grandson Mun-ui said: "The king and crown prince are still alive, yet uncle makes himself king—if Tang troops withdraw, what will become of us father and son?"
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Tae, set himself up as king and held the city with the army. Uija's grandson Mun-ui said, "The king and the crown prince are still alive, yet my uncle crowns himself. When the Tang armies leave, what will they do to my grandfather and father?"

sentences.zh: 與左右縋而出，民皆從之，泰不能止。

translations.literal: He and his attendants lowered themselves by rope and went out; the common people all followed; Tae could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: He and his men let themselves down by rope and went out. The townspeople streamed after them, and Tae could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 定方令士超堞立幟，泰開門降，定方執義慈、隆及小王孝演、酋長五十八人送京師，平其國五部、三十七郡、二百城，戶七十六萬。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered soldiers to raise banners on the ramparts; Tae opened the gates and surrendered; Dingfang seized Uija, Yong, the junior king Hyoyŏn, and fifty-eight chieftains and sent them to the capital; he pacified their state—five departments, thirty-seven commanderies, two hundred cities, seven hundred sixty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang had his men plant banners on the walls. Tae opened the gates and submitted. Dingfang sent Uija, Yong, the young prince Hyoyŏn, and fifty-eight chieftains to the capital. He pacified the realm: five departments, thirty-seven commanderies, two hundred cities, and seven hundred sixty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 乃析置熊津、馬韓、東明、金漣、德安五都督府，擢酋渠長治之。

translations.literal: He then subdivided and established five protectorates—Ungjin, Mahan, Dongming, Geumnyeon, and Deok-an—and promoted tribal chiefs to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: The land was carved into five protectorates—Ungjin, Mahan, Dongming, Geumnyeon, and Deok-an—and local chiefs were raised to govern them.

sentences.zh: 命郎將劉仁願守百濟城，左衛郎將王文度爲熊津都督。

translations.literal: He ordered Colonel Liu Renyuan to guard the Baekje city and Left Guard Colonel Wang Wendu to serve as protector of Ungjin.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Liu Renyuan was left to hold the Baekje capital; Wang Wendu of the Left Guard was named protector of Ungjin.

sentences.zh: 九月，定方以所俘見，詔釋不誅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Dingfang presented the captives; an edict released them without execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Dingfang presented his prisoners at court. An edict spared them from death.

sentences.zh: 義慈病死，贈衛尉卿，許舊臣赴臨，詔葬孫皓、陳叔寶墓左，授隆司稼卿。

translations.literal: Uija died of illness; he was posthumously made Commandant of the Palace Guards; former ministers were permitted to attend the mourning; an edict ordered burial to the left of the tombs of Sun Hao and Chen Shubao; Yong was appointed Director of Field Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Uija died of illness. He was posthumously named Commandant of the Palace Guards, and his former ministers were allowed to come to the rites. An edict had him buried to the left of the tombs of Sun Hao and Chen Shubao—the last kings of Wu and Chen—and Yong was made Director of Field Grain.

sentences.zh: 文度濟海卒，以劉仁軌代之。

translations.literal: Wendu died crossing the sea; Liu Rengui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu died on the crossing. Liu Rengui took his place.

sentences.zh: 璋從子福信嘗將兵，乃與浮屠道琛據周留城反，迎故王子扶餘豐於倭，立爲王。

translations.literal: Zhang's nephew Fukushin had once commanded troops; he then joined the Buddhist monk Dochim in seizing Zhouliu city and rebelling, welcomed the former prince Buyeo Pung from Wa, and installed him as king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's nephew Fukushin, once a field commander, joined the Buddhist monk Dochim in seizing Zhouliu and rising in revolt. They brought back the former prince Buyeo Pung from Wa and set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 西部皆應，引兵圍仁願。

translations.literal: The western districts all responded; they led troops to besiege Renyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The western districts rose with them, and their columns closed round Renyuan.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，仁軌發新羅兵往救，道琛立二壁熊津江，仁軌與新羅兵夾擊之，奔入壁，爭梁墮溺者萬人，新羅兵還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo, Rengui mobilized Silla troops to rescue; Dochim erected two ramparts on the Bear Ford River; Rengui and the Silla forces attacked from both sides; fleeing into the ramparts, ten thousand were crushed on the bridge and drowned; the Silla troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longshuo, Rengui called up Silla troops to relieve the siege. Dochim threw up two stockades on the Bear Ford River. Rengui and the Silla army struck from both banks. The rebels fled into the stockades; ten thousand were trampled on the bridge and drowned in the water. The Silla troops then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道琛保任孝城，自稱領軍將軍，福信稱霜岑將軍，告仁軌曰：「聞唐與新羅約，破百濟，無老孺皆殺之；

translations.literal: Dochim held Renshou city, styled himself General of the Vanguard Army; Fukushin styled himself General of Frost Ridge; they told Rengui: "We have heard that Tang and Silla agreed that when Baekje was broken, none old or young would be spared;
translations.idiomatic: Dochim held Renshou and called himself General of the Vanguard Army; Fukushin took the title General of Frost Ridge. They sent word to Rengui: "We hear that Tang and Silla have agreed: once Baekje falls, not even the aged or infants are to be spared;

sentences.zh: 畀以國。

translations.literal: and the state would be given to them;
translations.idiomatic: and the kingdom is to be handed to Silla;

sentences.zh: 我與受死，不若戰。」

translations.literal: We would rather fight than accept death.
translations.idiomatic: We would rather die fighting than submit to slaughter."

sentences.zh: 仁軌遣使齎書答說，道琛倨甚，館使者于外，嫚報曰：「使人官小，我，國大將，禮不當見。」

translations.literal: Rengui sent an envoy bearing a letter to persuade them; Dochim was very arrogant, lodged the envoy outside, and replied insolently: "The envoy's rank is low; I am the state's great general—by ritual I ought not to receive him."
translations.idiomatic: Rengui sent an envoy with a letter of reply and persuasion. Dochim was insufferably proud. He quartered the envoy outside the walls and answered with contempt: "Your man's office is petty. I am this state's great general. Propriety does not require me to see him."

sentences.zh: 徒遣之。

translations.literal: He merely sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the man off and would not admit him.

sentences.zh: 仁軌以衆少，乃休軍養威，請合新羅圖之。

translations.literal: Rengui, with few troops, rested the army to build morale and requested to join Silla in planning the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui's force was thin. He halted the army to recover its strength and asked to concert plans with Silla.

sentences.zh: 福信俄殺道琛，并其兵，豐不能制。

translations.literal: Before long Fukushin killed Dochim and absorbed his troops; Pung could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fukushin killed Dochim and took his soldiers under his own banner. Pung could no longer command him.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，仁願等破之熊津，拔支羅城，夜薄真峴，比明入之，斬首八百級，新羅餉道乃開。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, Renyuan and others defeated them at Bear Ford, took Jurira city, at night pressed close to True Cliff, entered at dawn, cut eight hundred heads; Silla's supply route was then opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year Renyuan and the others routed them at Bear Ford and took Jurira. By night they pressed True Cliff; at first light they were inside. Eight hundred heads were taken, and Silla's supply line at last lay open.

sentences.zh: 仁願請濟師，詔右威衛將軍孫仁師爲熊津道行軍總管，發齊兵七千往。

translations.literal: Renyuan requested troops across the sea; an edict named Right Awesome Guard General Sun Renshi commander-in-chief of the Bear Ford campaign and sent seven thousand Qi troops.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan asked for reinforcements from across the sea. An edict made Sun Renshi of the Right Awesome Guard commander-in-chief on the Bear Ford route and dispatched seven thousand men from Qi.

sentences.zh: 福信顓國，謀殺豐；

translations.literal: Fukushin monopolized the state and plotted to kill Pung;
translations.idiomatic: Fukushin seized the reins of power and plotted to kill Pung;

sentences.zh: 豐率親信斬福信，與高麗、倭連和。

translations.literal: Pung led his intimates to execute Fukushin and allied with Goguryeo and Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Pung rallied his trusted men, struck Fukushin down, and made common cause with Goguryeo and Wa.

sentences.zh: 仁願已得齊兵，士氣振，乃與新羅王金法敏率步騎，而遣劉仁軌率舟師，自熊津江偕進，趨周留城。

translations.literal: Renyuan had received the Qi troops; morale surged. He and Silla King Kim Beopmun led infantry and cavalry, while dispatching Liu Rengui with the fleet; together they advanced up the Bear Ford River toward Zhouliu city.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan now had the Qi reinforcements, and the army's spirit rose. He marched with Silla's King Kim Beopmun at the head of foot and horse, while Liu Rengui led the fleet. Up the Bear Ford River they went together, bearing down on Zhouliu.

sentences.zh: 豐衆屯白江口，四遇皆克，火四百艘；

translations.literal: Pung's host encamped at White River Mouth; in four encounters all were victories; four hundred vessels were burned;
translations.idiomatic: Pung's forces held White River Mouth. In four clashes they were broken every time; four hundred ships were put to the torch;

sentences.zh: 豐走不知所在。

translations.literal: Pung fled; no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: Pung fled. No one could say where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 偽王子扶餘忠勝、忠志率殘衆及倭人請命，諸城皆復。

translations.literal: The pretender princes Buyeo Jungseung and Jungji led the remnant host and Wa men to beg mercy; all cities were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The pretender princes Buyeo Jungseung and Jungji brought the survivors and the Wa troops to sue for quarter. City after city submitted again.

sentences.zh: 仁願勒軍還，留仁軌代守。

translations.literal: Renyuan led the army back and left Rengui to hold the post in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan marched home and left Rengui behind as his replacement.

sentences.zh: 帝以扶餘隆爲熊津都督，俾歸國，平新羅故憾，招還遺人。

translations.literal: The emperor made Buyeo Yong protector of Bear Ford, sent him home to his state, smoothed old grievances with Silla, and summoned back those who had fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Buyeo Yong protector of Bear Ford and sent him home to rule. Old scores with Silla were laid to rest, and scattered people were called back.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年，與新羅王會熊津城，刑白馬以盟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde, he met the Silla king at Bear Ford fortress; a white horse was slaughtered for the oath.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Linde he met the king of Silla at Bear Ford. They slew a white horse and swore the covenant.

sentences.zh: 仁軌爲盟辭曰：「往百濟先王，罔顧逆順，不敦鄰，不睦親，與高麗、倭共侵削新羅，破邑屠城。

translations.literal: Rengui spoke the covenant oath: "In times past the kings of Baekje, heedless of right and wrong, did not cultivate neighbors or keep kinship bonds; with Goguryeo and Wa they jointly invaded and carved away Silla, breaking towns and slaughtering cities.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui pronounced the oath of alliance: "Former kings of Baekje, blind to what was just, would not honor their neighbors or keep faith with kin. With Goguryeo and Wa they joined to strip Silla of its lands, razing towns and putting cities to the sword.

sentences.zh: 天子憐百姓無辜，命行人脩好，先王負險恃遐，侮慢弗恭。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven pitied the guiltless common people and sent envoys to restore amity; the former king relied on rugged terrain and distant seas, treating them with contempt and irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven pitied the innocent people and sent envoys to make peace. The late king trusted his cliffs and his distance from the court, and answered with scorn and insolence.

sentences.zh: 皇赫斯怒，是伐是夷。

translations.literal: The Emperor in his august wrath came to chastise and level them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor in his blazing anger marched forth to strike them down.

sentences.zh: 但興亡繼絕，王者通制，故立前太子隆爲熊津都督，守其祭祀，附杖新羅，長爲與國，結好除怨，恭天子命，永爲籓服。

translations.literal: Yet to restore what was fallen and continue what was cut off is the universal rule of true kings. Therefore the former crown prince Yong was installed as Protector of Bear Ford, to keep their sacrifices, lean upon Silla as a staff, and ever after be an allied state—ending enmity, forging friendship, revering the Son of Heaven's command, and forever remaining a tributary domain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to raise up what has fallen and to carry on a broken line is the way of a true king. For this reason the former crown prince Yong was set up as Protector of Bear Ford, to tend the ancestral rites, to lean on Silla as on a staff, and to stand forever as her ally—burying old hatred, binding new friendship, honoring the Son of Heaven's command, and remaining forever a vassal land.

sentences.zh: 右威衛將軍魯城縣公仁願，親臨厥盟，有貳其德，興兵動衆，明神監之，百殃是降，子孫不育，社稷無守，世世毋敢犯。」

translations.literal: Right Awesome Guard General, Duke of Lu County, Renyuan, personally witnessed this covenant. Should any turn their heart from its virtue, raise troops and move the multitude, the clear spirits will watch: a hundred calamities shall descend, their descendants shall not thrive, their altars shall have no keeper, and for generation after generation none may dare violate it."
translations.idiomatic: Right Awesome Guard General Renyuan, Duke of Lu County, stood witness to this oath. Whoever turns against its bond and takes up arms—the bright spirits are watching. A hundred disasters will fall; their line will fail; their altars will stand empty. Let no generation dare to break this pact."

sentences.zh: 乃作金書鐵契，藏新羅廟中。

translations.literal: They then made a covenant inscribed in gold on iron and stored it in Silla's temple.
translations.idiomatic: They drew up the pact in letters of gold on plates of iron and laid it up in Silla's ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 仁願等還，隆畏衆攜散，亦歸京師。

translations.literal: Renyuan and the others returned; Yong, fearing the people would scatter, also returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan and his officers went home. Yong, afraid his people would melt away, followed them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳時，進帶方郡王，遣歸籓。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era he was advanced to Prince of Daifang Commandery and sent back to the tributary state.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng period he was raised to Prince of Daifang Commandery and sent home to his domain.

sentences.zh: 是時，新羅強，隆不敢入舊國，寄治高麗死。

translations.literal: At that time Silla was strong; Yong dared not enter the old country, dwelt as a guest under Goguryeo, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Silla was then at the height of her power. Yong did not dare return to his ancestral lands. He lived as a guest in Goguryeo territory and died there.

sentences.zh: 武后又以其孫敬襲王，而其地已爲新羅、渤海靺鞨所分，百濟遂絕。

translations.literal: Empress Wu later had his grandson Gyeong succeed as king, but the land had already been divided between Silla and Bohai Mohe; Baekje thus ended.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu later installed his grandson Gyeong as king in name, but the country had already been carved up between Silla and the Mohe of Bohai. Baekje was no more.

sentences.zh: 新羅，弁韓苗裔也。

translations.literal: Silla were descendants of Byeonhan.
translations.idiomatic: Silla sprang from the line of Byeonhan.

sentences.zh: 居漢樂浪地，橫千里，縱三千里，東拒長人，東南日本，西百濟，南瀕海，北高麗。

translations.literal: They dwelt in former Han Lelang territory, a thousand li east-west and three thousand li north-south; east they bordered the Long People; southeast Japan; west Baekje; south the sea; north Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: They held the old Han territory of Lelang—roughly a thousand li across and three thousand from north to south. On the east lay the Long People; to the southeast, Japan; Baekje to the west; the sea to the south; Goguryeo to the north.

sentences.zh: 而王居金城，環八里所，衛兵三千人。

translations.literal: The king dwelt at Geumseong, encircling about eight li; palace guards numbered three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The king kept court at Geumseong, a walled circuit of some eight li, with three thousand guards at his gate.

sentences.zh: 謂城爲侵牟羅，邑在內曰喙評，外曰邑勒。

translations.literal: They called the city Seorabeol; settlements within were called hyeolpyeong, outside eupnok.
translations.idiomatic: Their capital they named Seorabeol. Towns within the walls were hyeolpyeong; those beyond were eupnok.

sentences.zh: 有喙評六，邑勒五十二。

translations.literal: There were six hyeolpyeong and fifty-two eupnok.
translations.idiomatic: Six hyeolpyeong and fifty-two eupnok made up the realm.

sentences.zh: 朝服尚白，好祠山神。

translations.literal: Court dress favored white; they delighted in sacrificing to mountain spirits.
translations.idiomatic: White was the color of court dress. They were devoted to the worship of mountain gods.

sentences.zh: 八月望日，大宴齎官吏，射。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of the eighth month they held a great feast, bestowing gifts on officials, and archery.
translations.idiomatic: On the full moon of the eighth month they gave a great banquet, rewarded their officers with gifts, and held an archery contest.

sentences.zh: 其建官，以親屬爲上，其族名第一骨、第二骨以自別。

translations.literal: In establishing offices, kin were placed highest; their clans were named First Bone and Second Bone to distinguish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing officials, blood kin came first. The nobility divided themselves into the First Bone and the Second Bone.

sentences.zh: 兄弟女、姑、姨、從姊妹，皆聘爲妻。

translations.literal: A man's sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, and female cousins were all taken as wives.
translations.idiomatic: A man might marry his sisters, his father's sisters, his mother's sisters, and his female cousins on either side.

sentences.zh: 王族爲第一骨，妻亦其族，生子皆爲第一骨，不娶第二骨女，雖娶，常爲妾媵。

translations.literal: The royal clan was First Bone; wives too were from their clan; children were all First Bone. They did not marry Second Bone women—or if they did, such wives remained concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house was First Bone. Its wives came from the same bone-rank, and every child born to them was First Bone. They did not wed Second Bone women; if one was taken, she remained a concubine only.

sentences.zh: 官有宰相、侍中、司農卿、太府令，凡十有七等，第二骨得爲之。

translations.literal: Offices included Chancellor, Palace Attendant, Director of the Granaries, and Grand Treasury Director—seventeen ranks in all, which Second Bone could hold.
translations.idiomatic: Their offices ran from Chancellor and Palace Attendant to Director of the Granaries and Grand Treasury Director—seventeen ranks in all, open to the Second Bone.

sentences.zh: 事必與衆議，號「和白」，一人異則罷。

translations.literal: Affairs had to be deliberated with the multitude, called "hwabaek"; one dissenting voice and it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Every weighty matter had to pass the council called "hwabaek." A single dissenting voice was enough to set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 宰相家不絕祿，奴僮三千人，甲兵牛馬豬稱之。

translations.literal: Chancellor households received perpetual stipends, three thousand slave-retainers, with armor, cattle, horses, and pigs to match.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor families drew stipends without end and kept three thousand bond-servants, with arms, cattle, horses, and swine in proportion.

sentences.zh: 畜牧海中山，須食乃射。

translations.literal: They pastured livestock on sea islands; they shot only when food was needed.
translations.idiomatic: They raised herds on islands in the sea and hunted only when meat was wanted.

sentences.zh: 息谷米於人，償不滿，庸爲奴婢。

translations.literal: If one lent grain at interest and repayment fell short, the debtor served as bondman or maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: Grain lent at interest, if not repaid in full, was collected in the labor of bondmen and maidservants.

sentences.zh: 王姓金，貴人姓朴，民無氏有名。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Kim; nobles bore Pak; commoners had no surname, only given names.
translations.idiomatic: The royal line was Kim; the great families were Pak. Ordinary people carried no clan name, only personal names.

sentences.zh: 食用柳杯若銅、瓦。

translations.literal: For eating they used willow cups like copper or tile.
translations.idiomatic: They ate from willow cups shaped like bronze or earthenware vessels.

sentences.zh: 元日相慶，是日拜日月神。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day they celebrate together; on that day they worship the sun and moon spirits.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the people feast together, and on that day they worship the spirits of the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 男子褐褲。

translations.literal: Men wear brown trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Men dress in brown hemp trousers.

sentences.zh: 婦長襦，見人必跪，則以手據地爲恭。

translations.literal: Women wear long jackets; when they see anyone they must kneel, then press their hands to the ground in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Women wear long jackets; when they meet anyone they kneel and press their hands to the ground in deference.

sentences.zh: 不粉黛，率美髮以繚首，以珠彩飾之。

translations.literal: They do not use powder or rouge; generally they bind their beautiful hair about the head and adorn it with pearls and colored ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: They wear no powder or rouge; as a rule they coil their fine hair about the head and deck it with pearls and colored trinkets.

sentences.zh: 男子翦發鬻，冒以黑巾。

translations.literal: Men cut their hair and sell it, covering their heads with black kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Men cut their hair short and sell it, then cover their heads with black kerchiefs.

sentences.zh: 市皆婦女貿販。

translations.literal: In the markets women do all the trading.
translations.idiomatic: Women handle all commerce in the markets.

sentences.zh: 冬則作灶堂中，夏以食置冰上。

translations.literal: In winter they build stoves in the hall; in summer they set food on ice.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they build hearths in the main hall; in summer they chill food on ice.

sentences.zh: 畜無羊，少驢、驘，多馬。

translations.literal: Among livestock there are no sheep, few donkeys and mules, and many horses.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no sheep, few donkeys or mules, and many horses.

sentences.zh: 馬雖高大，不善行。

translations.literal: Although the horses are tall and large, they do not travel well.
translations.idiomatic: Though their horses are tall and powerful, they are poor travelers.

sentences.zh: 長人者，人類長三丈，鋸牙鉤爪，黑毛覆身，不火食，噬禽獸，或搏人以食；

translations.literal: The Long Men are a humanoid race three zhang tall, with saw-like teeth and hooked claws, black fur covering their bodies; they do not eat by fire but devour birds and beasts, sometimes seizing people to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The Long Men are a people three zhang in height, with saw-edged teeth and hooked claws, their bodies shrouded in black fur; they eat no cooked food but tear apart birds and beasts, and sometimes seize human beings for food.

sentences.zh: 得婦人，以治衣服。

translations.literal: When they capture women, they use them to make clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When they take women captive, they set them to making garments.

sentences.zh: 其國連山數十里，有峽，固以鐵闔，號關門，新羅常屯弩士數千守之。

translations.literal: Their country runs along mountains for several tens of li; there is a gorge fortified with an iron barrier, called the Barrier Gate; Silla regularly stations several thousand crossbow troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Their land stretches along the mountains for dozens of li; a pass there is barred with an iron gate called the Barrier Gate, which Silla keeps garrisoned with several thousand crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 初，百濟伐高麗，來請救，悉兵往破之，自是相攻不置。

translations.literal: At first Baekje attacked Goguryeo and came requesting aid; Silla sent all its troops and defeated them; from then on they attacked each other without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Baekje attacked Goguryeo and appealed for help, Silla marched out in full force and routed them; thereafter the two states warred without respite.

sentences.zh: 後獲百濟王殺之，滋結怨。

translations.literal: Later they captured the king of Baekje and killed him, deepening the grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Later Silla captured the king of Baekje and put him to death, and the hatred between them only grew.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，王真平遣使者入朝，高祖詔通直散騎侍郎庾文素持節答齎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, King Jinpyeong sent envoys to court; Emperor Gaozu ordered Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Wensu to bear credentials in reply and bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, King Jinpyeong sent envoys to court, and Emperor Gaozu ordered Yu Wensu, Supervising Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, to return the visit with imperial credentials and gifts.

sentences.zh: 後三年，拜柱國，封樂浪郡王、新羅王。

translations.literal: Three years later he was appointed Grand General-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Prince of Lelang Commandery and King of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Jinpyeong was made Grand General-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Prince of Lelang Commandery and King of Silla.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，獻女樂二。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan they presented two female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguan they presented two female musicians to the court.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「比林邑獻鸚鵡，言思鄉，丐還，況於人乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "Recently Lin Yi presented a parrot that spoke of missing home and begged to be sent back—how much more so with people?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "Not long ago Lin Yi sent us a parrot that spoke of homesickness and begged to go home—how much more is this true of human beings?"

sentences.zh: 付使者歸之。

translations.literal: He entrusted them to the envoys to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the women over to the envoys to take home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，真平死，無子，立女善德爲王，大臣乙祭柄國。

translations.literal: That year Jinpyeong died without sons; his daughter Seondeok was made ruler, and the great minister I Jipyeong held state power.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jinpyeong died without a son, and his daughter Queen Seondeok was enthroned while the great minister I Jipyeong wielded the government.

sentences.zh: 詔贈真平左光祿大夫，賻物段二百。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously invested Jinpyeong as Left Grand Master of the Splendorous Hall and gave two hundred bolts of funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored Jinpyeong as Left Grand Master of the Splendorous Hall and granted two hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣使者冊善德襲父封，國人號聖祖皇姑。

translations.literal: In the ninth year envoys were sent to invest Seondeok in her father's titles; the people called her the Sacred Ancestress and Imperial Aunt.
