translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the court sent envoys to invest Queen Seondeok in her father's titles, and her people hailed her as the Sacred Ancestress and Imperial Aunt.

sentences.zh: 十七年，爲高麗、百濟所攻，使者來乞師，亦會帝親伐高麗，詔率兵以披虜勢。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, attacked by Goguryeo and Baekje, envoys came begging for troops; it also coincided with the emperor's personal campaign against Goguryeo, and an edict ordered Silla to raise troops to break the enemy's momentum.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, as Goguryeo and Baekje pressed their attack, Silla's envoys came pleading for troops; the timing also matched the emperor's own expedition against Goguryeo, and an edict ordered Silla to march and scatter the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 善德使兵五萬入高麗南鄙，拔水口城以聞。

translations.literal: Seondeok sent fifty thousand troops into Goguryeo's southern marches and captured Shuikou Fortress, reporting the victory.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Seondeok dispatched fifty thousand men into Goguryeo's southern borderlands, took Shuikou Fortress, and sent word of the victory.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，善德死，贈光祿大夫，而妹真德襲王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Seondeok died, was posthumously invested as Grand Master of Splendorous Affairs, and her younger sister Jindeok succeeded as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Queen Seondeok died and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendorous Affairs; her younger sister Queen Jindeok succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣子文王及弟伊贊子春秋來朝，拜文王左武衛將軍，春秋特進。

translations.literal: The next year she sent her son Munwang and her younger brother Ija's son Chunchu to court; Munwang was appointed Left Martial Guard General, and Chunchu was made Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she sent her son Munwang and her younger brother Ija's son Kim Chunchu to court; Munwang was appointed Left Martial Guard General and Chunchu was granted the honorary rank of Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 因請改章服，從中國制，內出珍服賜之。

translations.literal: They requested to change their ceremonial dress to follow the Chinese system; the inner court issued fine robes as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to adopt Chinese court dress, and the palace issued them splendid robes from the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 又詣國學觀釋奠、講論，帝賜所制《晉書》。

translations.literal: They also visited the Imperial Academy to observe the sacrifice to Confucius and hear lectures; the emperor bestowed his own compilation of the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: They also went to the Imperial Academy to witness the Confucian sacrifice and attend lectures, and the emperor gave them his own compilation of the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 辭歸，敕三品以上郊餞。

translations.literal: When they took leave to return, an edict ordered officials of the third rank and above to see them off at the suburban gate.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to depart, an edict commanded all officials of the third rank and above to give them a farewell feast outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽元年，攻百濟，破之，遣春秋子法敏入朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui of Emperor Gaozong, Silla attacked and defeated Baekje and sent Chunchu's son Beopmin to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui under Emperor Gaozong, Silla attacked Baekje, defeated it, and sent Chunchu's son Beopmin to court.

sentences.zh: 真德織錦爲頌以獻，曰：「巨唐開洪業，巍巍皇猷昌。

translations.literal: Jindeok wove a brocade hymn of praise to present, saying: "Great Tang opens its vast enterprise; august is the royal design in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Jindeok wove a brocade hymn of praise and presented it, reading: "Great Tang opens its vast enterprise; august is the royal design in splendor.

sentences.zh: 止戈成大定，興文繼百王。

translations.literal: Ceasing arms brings great settlement; raising culture continues the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: When the weapons are laid down, great peace is secured; when learning is exalted, the hundred kings live again.

sentences.zh: 統天崇雨施，治物體含章。

translations.literal: Governing Heaven, exalting rain's bounty; ordering the myriad things, embodying inner brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is embraced and rain's grace exalted; all things are governed, their inner pattern made manifest.

sentences.zh: 深仁諧日月，撫運邁時康。

translations.literal: Deep benevolence harmonizes sun and moon; ruling the age, surpassing timely peace.
translations.idiomatic: Deep benevolence brings sun and moon into harmony; ruling the age, he surpasses the peace of his time.

sentences.zh: 幡旗既赫赫，鉦鼓何鍠鍠。

translations.literal: Banners already blaze bright; bells and drums—how they ring and clang!
translations.idiomatic: Banners blaze in splendor; bells and drums thunder and clang.

sentences.zh: 外夷違命者，翦覆被天殃。

translations.literal: Barbarians of the outer realms who defy commands are cut down and overthrown, suffering Heaven's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Outland peoples who defy the throne are cut down and cast under, smitten by Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 淳風凝幽顯，遐邇競呈祥。

translations.literal: Pure winds congeal in hidden and manifest realms; far and near vie to present auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Pure customs settle over seen and unseen realms; near and far alike rush to offer auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 四時和玉燭，七耀巡萬方。

translations.literal: The four seasons harmonize with the jade candle; the seven luminaries tour the ten thousand directions.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons keep the jade candle's harmony; the seven luminaries wheel through the ten thousand realms.

sentences.zh: 維嶽降宰輔，維帝任忠良。

translations.literal: The paramount peak sends forth ministers; the emperor appoints loyal worthies.
translations.idiomatic: From the sacred peak ministers descend; the emperor entrusts the loyal and able.

sentences.zh: 三五成一德，昭我唐家唐。」

translations.literal: The Three and Five [sages] merge into one virtue—manifest our House of Tang!"
translations.idiomatic: The sages of the Three and Five ages unite in one virtue—glory to the House of Tang!"

sentences.zh: 帝美其意，擢法敏太府卿。

translations.literal: The emperor praised their intent and promoted Beopmin to Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired the sentiment and promoted Beopmin to Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 五年，真德死，帝爲舉哀，贈開府儀同三司，賜彩段三百，命太常丞張文收持節弔祭，以春秋襲王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Queen Jindeok died; the emperor held mourning for her, posthumously invested her as Grand Steward with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, gave three hundred bolts of colored silk, ordered Vice Director of Court Ceremonies Zhang Wenshou to bear credentials for condolence sacrifices, and had Chunchu succeed as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Queen Jindeok died; the emperor mourned her in person, posthumously honored her as Grand Steward with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, granted three hundred bolts of colored silk, and sent Zhang Wenshou, Vice Director of Court Ceremonies, with credentials to perform the condolence rites; Chunchu succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年，百濟、高麗、靺鞨共伐取其三十城。

translations.literal: The next year Baekje, Goguryeo, and Mohe jointly attacked and seized thirty of its cities.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Baekje, Goguryeo, and Mohe joined forces and captured thirty of Silla's cities.

sentences.zh: 使者來請救，帝命蘇定方討之，以春秋爲隅夷道行軍總管，遂平百濟。

translations.literal: Envoys came seeking rescue; the emperor ordered Su Dingfang to punish them and appointed Chunchu Campaign Commander-in-Chief on the Xieyi Road, thus pacifying Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys came pleading for aid; the emperor ordered Su Dingfang to chastise the invaders and made Chunchu Campaign Commander-in-Chief on the Xieyi Road, and Baekje was pacified.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，死，法敏襲王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he died; Beopmin succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longshuo Chunchu died, and Beopmin succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以其國爲雞林州大都督府，授法敏都督。

translations.literal: His state was made the Greater Area Command of Jilin Prefecture, and Beopmin was appointed Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Silla was made the Greater Area Command of Jilin Prefecture, and Beopmin was appointed its Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 咸亨五年，納高麗叛眾，略百濟地守之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianheng, Beopmin accepted Goguryeo rebel bands, seized Baekje territory, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianheng, Beopmin accepted Goguryeo rebel bands, seized Baekje territory, and held it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔削官爵，以其弟右驍衛員外大將軍、臨海郡公仁問為新羅王，自京師歸國。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry. An edict stripped Beopmin of his offices and titles and made his younger brother Inmun, supernumerary grand general of the Right Valiant Guard and Duke of Linhai Commandery, king of Silla, sending him home from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry. An edict stripped Beopmin of his offices and titles and made his younger brother Inmun, supernumerary grand general of the Right Valiant Guard and Duke of Linhai Commandery, king of Silla, sending him home from the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔劉仁軌為雞林道大總管，衛尉卿李弼、右領軍大將軍李謹行副之，發兵窮討。

translations.literal: An edict made Liu Rengui Grand Commander of the Jilin Route, with Li Bi, chamberlain for palace garrisons, and Li Jinxing, grand general of the Right Commanding Army, as his deputies, and troops were mobilized for a thorough punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Liu Rengui Grand Commander of the Jilin Route, with Li Bi, chamberlain for palace garrisons, and Li Jinxing, grand general of the Right Commanding Army, as his deputies, and troops were mobilized for a thorough punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 上元二年二月，仁軌破其眾於七重城，以靺鞨兵浮海略南境，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shangyuan, Rengui defeated their forces at Qizhong City. He sent Mohe troops by sea to raid the southern border, killing and capturing very many.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Shangyuan, Rengui defeated their forces at Qizhong City. He sent Mohe troops by sea to raid the southern border, killing and capturing very many.

sentences.zh: 詔李謹行為安東鎮撫大使，屯買肖城，三戰，虜皆北。

translations.literal: An edict made Li Jinxing Grand Commissioner for Pacification of Andong. He garrisoned Maixiao City, fought three battles, and the enemy were defeated each time.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Li Jinxing Grand Commissioner for Pacification of Andong. He garrisoned Maixiao City, fought three battles, and the enemy were defeated each time.

sentences.zh: 法敏遣使入朝謝罪，貢篚相望，仁問乃還，辭王，詔復法敏官爵。

translations.literal: Beopmin sent envoys to court to apologize for his crimes, and tribute baskets came one after another. Inmun then returned, declined the kingship, and an edict restored Beopmin's offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Beopmin sent envoys to court to apologize for his crimes, and tribute baskets came one after another. Inmun then returned, declined the kingship, and an edict restored Beopmin's offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 然多取百濟地，遂抵高麗南境矣。

translations.literal: Even so, Silla had taken much of Baekje's land and now reached Goguryeo's southern border.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Silla had taken much of Baekje's land and now reached Goguryeo's southern border.

sentences.zh: 置尚、良、康、熊、全、武、漢、朔、溟九州，州有都督，統郡十或二十，郡有大守，縣有小守。

translations.literal: It established nine provinces: Shang, Liang, Kang, Ung, Jeon, Mu, Han, Sak, and Myeong. Each province had an area commander and governed ten or twenty commanderies; each commandery had a grand governor, and each county had a lesser governor.
translations.idiomatic: It established nine provinces: Shang, Liang, Kang, Ung, Jeon, Mu, Han, Sak, and Myeong. Each province had an area commander and governed ten or twenty commanderies; each commandery had a grand governor, and each county had a lesser governor.

sentences.zh: 開耀元年，死，子政明襲王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyao, Beopmin died, and his son Jeongmyeong succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyao, Beopmin died, and his son Jeongmyeong succeeded as king.

sentences.zh: 遣使者朝，丐唐禮及它文辭，武后賜《吉凶禮》并文詞五十篇。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to court requesting Tang rites and other writings. Empress Wu bestowed the Rites for Auspicious and Inauspicious Occasions together with fifty literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to court requesting Tang rites and other writings. Empress Wu bestowed the Rites for Auspicious and Inauspicious Occasions together with fifty literary pieces.

sentences.zh: 死，子理洪襲王。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Ihong succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Ihong succeeded as king.

sentences.zh: 死，弟興光襲王。

translations.literal: When Ihong died, his younger brother Heunggwang succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: When Ihong died, his younger brother Heunggwang succeeded as king.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元中，數入朝，獻果下馬、朝霞紬、魚牙紬、海豹皮。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong they repeatedly came to court, presenting underslung horses, Chaoxia silk, fish-tooth silk, and seal pelts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong they came to court repeatedly, presenting pony horses, Chaoxia silk, fish-tooth silk, and seal pelts.

sentences.zh: 又獻二女，帝曰：「女皆王姑姊妹，違本俗，別所親，朕不忍留。」

translations.literal: They again presented two women; the emperor said: "These women are the king's paternal aunts and sisters—in violation of their native custom, torn from those dear to them; I cannot bear to keep them."
translations.idiomatic: They again presented two women; the emperor said, "These women are the king's paternal aunts and sisters. To tear them from their kin defies their own customs; I cannot bear to keep them."

sentences.zh: 厚賜還之。

translations.literal: He gave them generous gifts and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them rich gifts and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 又遣子弟入太學學經術。

translations.literal: They also sent princes and sons to study the classics in the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent royal sons and younger kinsmen to the Grand Academy to study the classics.

sentences.zh: 帝間賜興光瑞文錦、五色羅、紫繡紋袍、金銀精器。

translations.literal: The emperor from time to time bestowed on Xingguang auspicious-pattern brocade, five-colored gauze, purple embroidered patterned robes, and fine gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time the emperor granted Xingguang brocades of auspicious weave, five-colored gauzes, purple embroidered robes, and fine gold and silver wares.

sentences.zh: 興光亦上異狗馬、黃金、美髢諸物。

translations.literal: Xingguang also presented in tribute exotic dogs and horses, gold, fine wigs, and various other things.
translations.idiomatic: Xingguang likewise sent tribute of rare dogs and horses, gold, fine wigs, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 初，渤海靺鞨掠登州，興光擊走之，帝進興光甯海軍大使，使攻靺鞨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bohai Mohe raided Dengzhou; Xingguang attacked and drove them off. The emperor promoted Xingguang to ambassador of the Ninghai Army and had him attack the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Mohe from Bohai had raided Dengzhou; Xingguang struck and drove them back. The emperor advanced him to ambassador of the Ninghai Army and ordered him to attack the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 二十五年死，帝尤悼之，贈太子太保，命邢璹以鴻臚少卿弔祭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; the emperor mourned him especially, posthumously invested him as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and ordered Xing Suo, as Vice Director of the Court for State Guest Ceremonies, to offer condolence sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died; the emperor grieved for him deeply, posthumously honored him as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and sent Xing Suo, Vice Director of the Court for State Guest Ceremonies, to perform the condolence rites.

sentences.zh: 子承慶襲王，詔璹曰：「新羅號君子國，知《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: His son Seonggyeong succeeded as king. An edict told Suo: "Silla is called the Land of Gentlemen and knows the Book of Poetry and the Book of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: His son Seonggyeong succeeded to the throne. An edict told Suo, "Silla is called the Land of Gentlemen; its people know the Book of Poetry and the Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 以卿惇儒，故持節往，宜演經誼，使知大國之盛。」

translations.literal: Because you are sincere and learned in the Ru classics, you are sent bearing credentials. You should expound the meaning of the classics and make them know the greatness of the great state."
translations.idiomatic: Because you are sincere and steeped in the classics, you go bearing credentials. Expound the meaning of the canon and let them know the grandeur of the great empire."

sentences.zh: 又以國人善棋，詔率府兵曹參軍楊季鷹爲副。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the people of the country are skilled at chess, an edict appointed Yang Jiying, Army-Cavalry Participating Officer of the Pitcher Palace Office, as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because the countrymen excel at chess, an edict named Yang Jiying, Army-Cavalry Participating Officer of the Pitcher Palace Office, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 國高弈皆出其下，於是厚遺使者金寶。

translations.literal: The state's master players were all beneath him; thereupon they richly gifted the envoys with gold and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom's finest players were all beneath him; the court then lavished gold and treasures on the envoys.

sentences.zh: 俄冊其妻朴爲妃。

translations.literal: Soon his wife Pak was invested as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his wife, of the Pak clan, was invested as royal consort.

sentences.zh: 承慶死，詔使者臨吊，以其弟憲英嗣王。

translations.literal: Seonggyeong died; an edict ordered the envoy to attend condolences, and his younger brother Heonnyeong succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: When Seonggyeong died, an edict ordered the envoy to attend the mourning, and his younger brother Heonnyeong succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝在蜀，遣使溯江至成都朝正月。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in Shu, [Silla] sent envoys upriver to Chengdu for the first-month court audience.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was in Shu, envoys went upriver to Chengdu for the New Year's court audience.

sentences.zh: 大曆初，憲英死，子乾運立，甫丱，遣金隱居入朝待命。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era Heonnyeong died; his son Geonun was installed, just past the cap-wearing age; he sent Kim Eunggeo to court to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali era Heonnyeong died; his son Geonun succeeded, still a child just come of age, and sent Kim Eunggeo to court to await imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 詔倉部郎中歸崇敬往吊，監察御史陸珽、顧愔爲副冊授之，并母金爲太妃。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gui Chongjing, Director in the Ministry of Revenue, to go and condole; Supervising Censors Lu Ting and Gu Yin as deputies to invest him; together his mother Kim was made Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Gui Chongjing of the Ministry of Revenue to offer condolences, with Supervising Censors Lu Ting and Gu Yin as deputies to invest the new king; his mother, of the Kim clan, was made Grand Consort as well.

sentences.zh: 會其宰相爭權相攻，國大亂，三歲乃定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers contended for power and attacked one another; the state fell into great disorder, and only after three years was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the chief ministers fought one another for power; the realm fell into turmoil and was not settled until three years had passed.

sentences.zh: 於是，歲朝獻。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute missions came each year.
translations.idiomatic: After that they sent tribute to court every year.

sentences.zh: 建中四年死，無子，國人共立宰相金良相嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong he died without sons; the people jointly installed chief minister Kim Yangsang to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianzhong he died without an heir; the people together raised the chief minister Kim Yangsang to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，遣戶部郎中蓋塤持節命之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan the emperor sent Gai Xun, Director in the Ministry of Revenue, bearing credentials to appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan the court sent Gai Xun of the Ministry of Revenue with credentials to invest him.

sentences.zh: 是年死，立良相從父弟敬信襲王。

translations.literal: That same year he died; Kim Yangsang's younger male cousin Gyeongsin succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died; Yangsang's younger cousin Gyeongsin succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四年，死，無子，立嫡孫俊邕。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died without sons; the direct grandson Junyeong was installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died without an heir; his eldest grandson Junyeong was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣司封郎中韋丹持冊，未至，俊邕死，丹還。

translations.literal: The next year Wei Dan, Director in the Ministry of Civil Appointments, was sent bearing investiture documents; before he arrived Junyeong died and Dan returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wei Dan of the Ministry of Civil Appointments was sent with the investiture patent; before he arrived Junyeong died, and Dan turned back.

sentences.zh: 子重興立，永貞元年，詔兵部郎中元季方冊命。

translations.literal: His son Junggung was installed; in the first year of Yongzhen an edict ordered Yuan Jifang, Director in the Ministry of War, to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junggung succeeded; in the first year of Yongzhen an edict sent Yuan Jifang of the Ministry of War to invest him.

sentences.zh: 後三年，使者金力奇來謝，且言：「往歲冊故主俊邕爲主，母申太妃，妻叔妃，而俊邕不幸，冊今留省中，臣請授以歸。」

translations.literal: Three years later the envoy Kim Irlyeok came to give thanks and said: "In former years we invested the late lord Junyeong as ruler; his mother was made Grand Consort Shin, his wife Consort Sok; but Junyeong met misfortune. The investiture documents remain in your department; your subject asks to receive them and return."
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the envoy Kim Irlyeok came to give thanks and said, "In former years the late lord Junyeong was invested as king; his mother was made Grand Consort Shin and his wife Consort Sok; but Junyeong met an untimely end. The patent still rests in your ministry; I beg leave to receive it and carry it home."

sentences.zh: 又爲其宰相金彥升、金仲恭、王之弟蘇金添明丐門戟，詔皆可。

translations.literal: He also requested ceremonial gate-halberds for chief ministers Kim Eomsung and Kim Jung-gong and for the king's younger brother Su Kim Cheonmyeong; the edict approved all.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for ceremonial gate-halberds for the chief ministers Kim Eomsung and Kim Jung-gong and for the king's younger brother Su Kim Cheonmyeong; the edict granted every request.

sentences.zh: 凡再朝貢。

translations.literal: In all they came to court twice with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In all they presented tribute at court twice.

sentences.zh: 七年死，彥升立，來告喪，命職方員外郎崔廷吊，且命新王，以妻貞爲妃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; Eomsung was installed and came to announce the mourning. Cui Ting, Auxiliary Director in the Ministry of Works, was ordered to condole and invest the new king; his wife Jeong was made consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died; Eomsung succeeded and came to announce the mourning. Cui Ting, Auxiliary Director in the Ministry of Works, was sent to condole and invest the new king; Eomsung's wife Jeong was made royal consort.

sentences.zh: 長慶、寶曆間，再遣使者來朝，留宿衛。

translations.literal: Between Changqing and Baoli they twice sent envoys to court, who remained as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Changqing and Baoli reigns they twice sent envoys to court, who were kept on as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 彥升死，子景徽立。

translations.literal: Eomsung died; his son Gyeonghui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Eomsung died, his son Gyeonghui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大和五年，以太子左諭德源寂冊吊如儀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dahe, Yuan Ji, Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was sent to invest and condole according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dahe, Yuan Ji, Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was dispatched to invest the new king and perform the condolence rites in due form.

sentences.zh: 開成初，遣子義琮謝，願留衛，見聽，明年遣之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng [the king] sent his son Eichong to give thanks, asking to remain on guard; permission was granted; the next year he was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era the king sent his son Eichong to give thanks and asked that he remain on palace guard; the request was granted, and the next year he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 五年，鴻臚寺籍質子及學生歲滿者一百五人，皆還之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Court for State Guest Ceremonies registered one hundred five hostage princes and students whose year was complete; all were sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Court for State Guest Ceremonies listed one hundred five royal hostages and students whose term was complete; all were sent home.

sentences.zh: 有張保皋、鄭年者，皆善鬥戰，工用槍。

translations.literal: There were Zhang Baogao and Zheng Nian, both skilled in combat and adept with the spear.
translations.idiomatic: There were Zhang Baogao and Zheng Nian, both expert fighters and masters of the spear.

sentences.zh: 年復能沒海，履其地五十里不噎，角其勇健，保皋不及也。

translations.literal: Nian could moreover dive into the sea and travel fifty li along the bottom without choking; when they matched their courage and vigor, Baogao could not equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Nian could also dive beneath the sea and walk fifty li along the seabed without drawing breath; matched for boldness and strength, Baogao was not his equal.

sentences.zh: 年以兄呼保皋，保皋以齒，年以藝，常不相下。

translations.literal: Nian called Baogao "elder brother"; Baogao [yielded] by age, Nian by skill—they were constantly unwilling to yield to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Nian called Baogao "elder brother"; Baogao claimed precedence by age, Nian by skill—and neither would yield to the other.

sentences.zh: 自其國皆來爲武甯軍小將。

translations.literal: Both came from their country to serve as junior officers in the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Both had come from Silla to serve as junior officers in the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 後保皋歸新羅，謁其王曰：「遍中國以新羅人爲奴婢，願得鎮清海，使賊不得掠人西去。」

translations.literal: Later Baogao returned to Silla and addressed the king: "Throughout China Silla people are made slaves; I wish to garrison Cheonghae so that bandits may not carry people off westward."
translations.idiomatic: Later Baogao returned to Silla and said to the king, "All across China Silla people are sold into bondage; grant me command of Cheonghae so pirates may no longer carry our people westward into slavery."

sentences.zh: 清海，海路之要也。

translations.literal: Cheonghae is the strategic point of the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: Cheonghae commands the sea lanes.

sentences.zh: 王與保皋萬人守之。

translations.literal: The king gave Baogao ten thousand men to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: The king gave Baogao ten thousand men to hold it.

sentences.zh: 自大和後，海上無鬻新羅人者。

translations.literal: From the Dahe era onward, on the sea no one sold Silla people.
translations.idiomatic: From the Dahe era onward, Silla people were no longer sold on the seas.

sentences.zh: 保皋既貴于其國，年饑寒客漣水，一日謂戍主馮元規曰：「我欲東歸，乞食于張保皋。」

translations.literal: After Baogao had risen high in his state, Nian, hungry and cold, lodged at Lianshui; one day he said to Garrison Commander Feng Yuangui: "I wish to go east and beg food from Zhang Baogao."
translations.idiomatic: Once Baogao had grown powerful at home, Nian, hungry and in rags, was staying at Lianshui; one day he told the garrison commander Feng Yuangui, "I mean to go east and beg a meal of Zhang Baogao."

sentences.zh: 元規曰：「若與保皋所負何如？

translations.literal: Yuangui said: "Compared with what you owe Baogao, how will it go?
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui said, "What of the score you owe Baogao?

sentences.zh: 奈何取死其手？」

translations.literal: Why seek death at his hands?"
translations.idiomatic: Why go seek your death at his hands?"

sentences.zh: 年曰：「饑寒死，不如兵死快，況死故鄉邪！」

translations.literal: Nian said: "To die of cold and hunger is not so swift as death in battle—and to die in one's homeland besides!"
translations.idiomatic: Nian said, "To die of hunger and cold is slower than to die by the sword—and what better place to die than one's own country!"

sentences.zh: 年遂去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nian departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that Nian set out.

sentences.zh: 至，謁保皋，飲之極歡。

translations.literal: When he arrived he called on Baogao, who entertained him with the greatest conviviality.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he visited Baogao, who feasted him with the greatest warmth.

sentences.zh: 飲未卒，聞大臣殺其王，國亂無主。

translations.literal: Before the drinking was finished, he heard that great ministers had killed the king and the state was in turmoil without a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Before the cups were empty, word came that great ministers had killed the king; the realm was in turmoil and leaderless.

sentences.zh: 保皋分兵五千人與年，持年泣曰：「非子不能平禍難。」

translations.literal: Baogao divided five thousand troops to give Nian, took Nian's hand and wept: "Only you can put this disaster to rights."
translations.idiomatic: Baogao gave Nian five thousand men, took his hand, and wept: "Only you can end this calamity."

sentences.zh: 年至其國，誅反者，立王以報。

translations.literal: When Nian reached the country he executed the rebels and installed a king to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Nian reached Silla, executed the rebels, enthroned a king, and sent word back.

sentences.zh: 王遂召保皋爲相，以年代守清海。

translations.literal: The king then summoned Baogao to be chief minister and had Nian guard Cheonghae in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The king then summoned Baogao to serve as chief minister and had Nian hold Cheonghae in his place.

sentences.zh: 會昌後，朝貢不復至。

translations.literal: After the Huichang era tribute missions no longer came.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huichang era tribute missions ceased to arrive.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：杜牧稱：「安思順爲朔方節度時，郭汾陽、李臨淮俱爲牙門都將，二人不相能，雖同盤飲食，常睇相視，不交一言。

translations.literal: Praise commentary says: Du Mu observed: "When An Sishun was military commissioner of Shuofang, Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi were both gate-generals of the headquarters; the two could not get on. Though they shared a plate at meals, they would often glare at each other across it and exchange not a word.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Du Mu wrote, "When An Sishun held Shuofang as military commissioner, Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi were both headquarters gate-generals; the two were at odds. Though they ate from the same dish, they would glare across it and never speak a word to each other.

sentences.zh: 及汾陽代思順，臨淮欲亡去，計未決。

translations.literal: When Fenyang replaced Sishun, Linhuai wished to flee but had not yet settled on a plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi succeeded An Sishun as commissioner, Li Guangbi wanted to abscond but could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 旬日，詔臨淮分汾陽半兵東出趙、魏，臨淮入請曰：『一死固甘，乞免妻子。』

translations.literal: Within ten days, an edict ordered Linhuai to detach half of Fenyang's troops and march east into Zhao and Wei; Linhuai entered to plead: "Death itself I would gladly accept; I beg only that my wife and children be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later the throne ordered Li Guangbi to take half of Guo Ziyi's army and advance east against Zhao and Wei. Li Guangbi came in person to plead: "I would willingly die—only spare my wife and children."

sentences.zh: 汾陽趨下，持手上堂，曰：'今國亂主遷，非公不能東伐，豈懷私忿時邪？

translations.literal: Fenyang hurried down, took his hand, and led him into the hall, saying: "The realm is in turmoil and the sovereign has been driven away; none but you, sir, can march east to campaign—how could this be the hour to harbor private resentment?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi rushed down, seized his hand, and led him upstairs. "The empire is in chaos and the Son of Heaven has fled the capital," he said. "No one but you can lead the eastern campaign. How can this be a time for private grudges?"

sentences.zh: '及別，執手泣涕，相勉以忠義，訖平劇盜，實二公之力。

translations.literal: When they parted, they clasped hands and wept, urging one another on in loyalty and righteousness; when the fierce rebels were at last pacified, it was truly the merit of these two lords.
translations.idiomatic: At their leave-taking they grasped hands and wept, exhorting each other to serve with loyalty and honor. The final defeat of the great rebellion was, in truth, the work of these two men.

sentences.zh: 知其心不叛，知其心，難也；

translations.literal: To know that his heart would not rebel—to know his heart—is difficult;
translations.idiomatic: To know that a man will not turn traitor—to know his heart—is hard;

sentences.zh: 忿必見短，知其材，益難也。

translations.literal: when angered one necessarily shows shortcomings; to know his capacity is still more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: anger lays bare a man's faults; to know his true ability is harder still.

sentences.zh: 此保皋與汾陽之賢等耳。

translations.literal: In this, Baogao and Fenyang were equally worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Here Zhang Baogao and Guo Ziyi were men of equal wisdom.

sentences.zh: 年投保皋必曰：'彼貴我賤，我降下之，不宜以舊忿殺我。

translations.literal: Each year when he placed himself in Baogao's power, Nian was sure to say: "He is lofty and I am lowly; I have humbled myself before him—he ought not to kill me over old resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Every year when he placed himself in Zhang Baogao's hands, Nian would say, "He is high and I am low; I have made myself submissive. He should not kill me for an old grudge."

sentences.zh: '保皋果不殺，人之常情也。

translations.literal: Baogao indeed did not kill him—this is the ordinary disposition of men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baogao in fact did not kill him. That is human nature.

sentences.zh: 臨淮請死於汾陽，亦人之常情也。

translations.literal: Linhuai asked death of Fenyang—this too is the ordinary disposition of men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi begging Guo Ziyi to take his life is human nature as well.

sentences.zh: 保皋任年，事出於己，年且寒饑，易爲感動。

translations.literal: Baogao had Nian in his charge and the affair arose from himself; Nian was moreover cold and hungry, and thus easily moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baogao held Nian's fate in his own hands, and Nian was cold and starving besides—he was easily swayed.

sentences.zh: 汾陽、臨淮，平生亢立，臨淮之命，出於天子。

translations.literal: Fenyang and Linhuai had stood proud all their lives, yet Linhuai's commission came from the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi had been proud equals all their lives, yet Li Guangbi's orders came from the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 榷於保皋，汾陽爲優。

translations.literal: Weighed against Baogao, Fenyang was superior.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Zhang Baogao's case, Guo Ziyi comes out the better.

sentences.zh: 此乃聖賢遲疑成敗之際也。

translations.literal: This is precisely the moment when sages and worthies hesitate between success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the very moment when the wise waver between triumph and disaster.

sentences.zh: 世稱周、邵爲百代之師，周公擁孺子而邵公疑之，以周公之聖，邵公之賢，少事文王，老佐武王，能平天下，周公之心，邵公且不知之。

translations.literal: The age calls Duke Zhou and the Duke of Shao teachers for a hundred generations; Duke Zhou embraced the infant sovereign and the Duke of Shao doubted him—with Duke Zhou's sagacity and the Duke of Shao's worthiness, serving King Wen in youth and aiding King Wu in old age, able to pacify All-under-Heaven—yet the Duke of Shao did not even know Duke Zhou's heart.
translations.idiomatic: The world hails the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao as masters for all ages. The Duke of Zhou held the young ruler in his arms, and the Duke of Shao suspected him. For all the Duke of Zhou's sanctity and the Duke of Shao's excellence—for all their service to King Wen in youth and King Wu in age, and their power to pacify the realm—the Duke of Shao still could not read the Duke of Zhou's mind.

sentences.zh: 苟有仁義之心，不資以明，雖邵公尚爾，況其下哉！」

translations.literal: If one harbors a heart of humaneness and righteousness yet is not aided by clarity, even the Duke of Shao was still thus—how much more those below him!
translations.idiomatic: Even with a heart full of benevolence and righteousness, without clear insight one cannot see through another soul. If the Duke of Shao was liable to such error, what hope for lesser men?"

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，不以怨毒相槊，而先國家之憂，晉有祁奚，唐有汾陽、保皋，孰謂夷無人哉！

translations.literal: Alas! Not to cross spears in envenomed hatred but to put the state's sorrow first—in Jin there was Qi Xi; in Tang, Fenyang and Baogao—who shall say the barbarians have no men of worth!
translations.idiomatic: Ah! To forgo mutual hatred and put the nation first: Jin had Qi Xi; Tang had Guo Ziyi and Zhang Baogao. Who will say that among the "barbarians" there are no great men?

sentences.zh: 倭，日本

translations.literal: Wa—Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Wa, or Japan.

sentences.zh: 日本，古倭奴也。

translations.literal: Japan is the old Wō-nú.
translations.idiomatic: Japan is ancient Wa.

sentences.zh: 去京師萬四千里，直新羅東南，在海中，島而居，東西五月行，南北三月行。

translations.literal: It lies fourteen thousand li from the capital, due southeast of Silla, amid the sea, dwelling on islands; east to west is a voyage of five months, north to south of three months.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen thousand li from the capital, it lies due southeast of Silla, in the ocean, on island shores. A voyage from east to west takes five months; from north to south, three.

sentences.zh: 國無城郛，聯木爲柵落，以草茨屋。

translations.literal: The state has no walled cities; it joins timber into palisade enclosures and roofs houses with thatch.
translations.idiomatic: The country has no walled towns. Villages are timber palisades; roofs are thatched.

sentences.zh: 左右小島五十餘，皆自名國，而臣附之。

translations.literal: More than fifty small islands to left and right each call itself a state and attaches itself in vassalage.
translations.idiomatic: Some fifty-odd lesser isles to either side each claims the name of a realm and renders submission.

sentences.zh: 置本率一人，檢察諸部。

translations.literal: It appoints one Chief Commander of the Realm to inspect all the divisions.
translations.idiomatic: A single supreme overseer is set over the districts to inspect them all.

sentences.zh: 其俗多女少男，有文字，尚浮屠法。

translations.literal: Its customs have many women and few men; it has writing and esteems the Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: Women outnumber men. They have a script and honor the Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 其官十有二等。

translations.literal: Its offices number twelve grades.
translations.idiomatic: There are twelve ranks of office.

sentences.zh: 其王姓阿每氏，自言初主號天御中主，至彥瀲，凡三十二世，皆以「尊」爲號，居築紫城。

translations.literal: The royal surname is the Ame clan; they say the first ruler was styled Celestial Sovereign in the Center; down to Hatsuse, altogether thirty-two reigns, all taking "Sovereign" as title, dwelling at Tsukushi Castle.
translations.idiomatic: Kings bear the surname of the Ame clan. They claim their first ruler was called Heaven's Central Lord. Down to Hatsuse there were thirty-two reigns, each styled "Sovereign," with the seat at Tsukushi Castle.

sentences.zh: 彥瀲子神武立，更以「天皇」爲號，徙治大和州。

translations.literal: Hatsuse's son Jimmu ascended, further taking "Heavenly Sovereign" as title, and moved the seat to govern Yamato Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hatsuse's son Jimmu came to the throne, adopted the title "Emperor of Heaven," and moved the capital to Yamato.

sentences.zh: 次曰綏靖，次安寧，次懿德，次孝昭，次天安，次孝靈，次孝元，次開化，次崇神，次垂仁，次景行，次成務，次仲哀。

translations.literal: Next came Suizei, then Annei, Itoku, Kōshō, Ten'an, Kōrei, Kōgen, Kaika, Sujin, Suinin, Keikō, Seimu, and Chūai.
translations.idiomatic: There followed Suizei, Annei, Itoku, Kōshō, Ten'an, Kōrei, Kōgen, Kaika, Sujin, Suinin, Keikō, Seimu, and Chūai.

sentences.zh: 仲哀死，以開化曾孫女神功爲王。

translations.literal: When Chūai died, a great-granddaughter of Kaika, the female Jingū, was made sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: At Chūai's death, Kaika's great-granddaughter—the empress Jingū—was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 次應神，次仁德，次履中，次反正，次允恭，次安康，次雄略，次清寧，次顯宗，次仁賢，次武烈，次繼體，次安閒，次宣化，次欽明。

translations.literal: Next came Ōjin, Nintoku, Richū, Hanzei, Ingyō, Ankō, Yūryaku, Seinei, Kenzō, Ninken, Buretsu, Keitai, Ankan, Senka, and Kinmei.
translations.idiomatic: There followed Ōjin, Nintoku, Richū, Hanzei, Ingyō, Ankō, Yūryaku, Seinei, Kenzō, Ninken, Buretsu, Keitai, Ankan, Senka, and Kinmei.

sentences.zh: 欽明之十一年，直梁承聖元年。

translations.literal: The eleventh year of Kinmei corresponded to the first year of Liang Chengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kinmei's eleventh year fell in the first year of Liang Chengsheng.

sentences.zh: 次海達。

translations.literal: Next came Haitatsu.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Haitatsu.

sentences.zh: 次用明，亦曰目多利思比孤，直隋開皇末，始與中國通。

translations.literal: Next Yōmei, also called Mutsu-tori-shi-hi-ko; at the end of Sui Kaihuang, tribute relations with China began.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Yōmei, also known as Mutsuhitoshihiko. At the close of Kaihuang in Sui, they first opened contact with China.

sentences.zh: 次崇峻。

translations.literal: Next came Sushun.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Sushun.

sentences.zh: 崇峻死，欽明之孫女雄古立。

translations.literal: When Sushun died, a granddaughter of Kinmei, the woman Kōgoku, ascended.
translations.idiomatic: At Sushun's death, Kinmei's granddaughter Kōgoku—the female sovereign—came to the throne.

sentences.zh: 次舒明，次皇極。

translations.literal: Next came Shōmei, then Kōgyoku.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Shōmei, then Empress Saimei.

sentences.zh: 其俗椎髻，無冠帶，跣以行，幅巾蔽後，貴者冒錦；

translations.literal: Their custom is topknots, no caps or belts; they go barefoot, with headcloth covering the back; the noble wear brocade on the head;
translations.idiomatic: Men wear topknots, neither cap nor belt, and walk barefoot. A cloth wraps the back of the head; the noble wind brocade about it;

sentences.zh: 婦人衣純色裙，長腰襦，結髮於後。

translations.literal: Women wear plain-colored skirts, long jackets reaching the waist, hair bound behind.
translations.idiomatic: Women dress in solid-colored skirts with long hip-length jackets, hair gathered at the back.

sentences.zh: 至煬帝，賜其民錦線冠，飾以金玉，文布爲衣，左右佩銀蘤長八寸，以多少明貴賤。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Yang, the people were granted brocade-thread caps adorned with gold and jade, patterned cloth for garments, and silver blossoms eight inches long worn at left and right—the number marking noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang they were given brocade caps set with gold and jade, patterned cloth for dress, and silver floral ornaments eight inches long worn on either side—rank shown by how many one might wear.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀五年，遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan of Taizong, an envoy was sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taizong's Zhenguan era, Japan sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 帝矜其遠，詔有司毋拘歲貢。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied their distance and ordered the authorities not to hold them to annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by how far they had come, ordered officials not to bind them to yearly tribute.

sentences.zh: 遣新州刺史高仁表往諭，與王爭禮不平，不肯宣天子命而還。

translations.literal: He sent Gao Renbiao, prefect of Xinzhou, to instruct them; he quarreled with the king over ritual precedence, would not proclaim the Son of Heaven's command, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Gao Renbiao, prefect of Xinzhou, to instruct them. He disputed ceremonial precedence with the king, refused to deliver the imperial message, and came back.

sentences.zh: 久之，更附新羅使者上書。

translations.literal: After a long while, they again attached themselves to Silla's envoys in memorializing the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After some years they once more submitted memorials through Silla's embassy.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，其王孝德即位，改元曰白雉，獻虎魄大如斗，碼硇若五升器。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, its king Kōtoku ascended, changed the era name to Hakuchi, and presented a lump of amber as large as a peck-measure and carnelian like a five-pint vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui, King Kōtoku came to the throne, proclaimed the era Hakuchi, and sent tribute: a mass of amber the size of a bushel measure and agate the size of a five-pint jar.

sentences.zh: 時新羅爲高麗、百濟所暴，高宗賜璽書，令出兵援新羅。

translations.literal: At the time Silla was ravaged by Koguryŏ and Paekche; Gaozong bestowed an imperial letter and ordered troops sent to relieve Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Silla was then suffering assault from Koguryŏ and Paekche. Emperor Gaozong issued a sealed edict ordering Japan to march and aid Silla.

sentences.zh: 未幾孝德死，其子天豐財立。

translations.literal: Before long Kōtoku died; his son Ten Hōzai ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kōtoku died, and his son Ten Hōzai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 死，子天智立。

translations.literal: He died; his son Tenchi ascended.
translations.idiomatic: He died in turn, and his son Tenchi took the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年，使者與蝦蛦人偕朝。

translations.literal: The next year, envoys came to court together with the Emishi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year their envoys arrived at court alongside men of the Emishi.

sentences.zh: 蝦蛦亦居海島中，其使者須長四尺許，珥箭於首，令人戴瓠立數十步，射無不中。

translations.literal: The Emishi also dwell among sea islands; their envoys had beards some four feet long, arrows thrust through their ears; they had a man wear a gourd on his head and stand several tens of paces away—the shot never missed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emishi too live on islands in the sea. Their envoys wore beards nearly four feet in length and stuck arrows through their earlobes. They set a man wearing a gourd on his head tens of paces off and never missed with a shot.

sentences.zh: 天智死，子天武立。

translations.literal: Tenchi died; his son Tenmu ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Tenchi died, and his son Tenmu ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 死，子總持立。

translations.literal: He died; his son Jito ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Tenmu died in turn, and his son Jito took the throne.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，遣使賀平高麗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianhe, envoys were sent to congratulate the pacification of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianhe, Japan sent envoys to congratulate the court on the conquest of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 後稍習夏音，惡倭名，更號日本。

translations.literal: Later they gradually learned the sounds of Xia, hated the name Wa, and changed their designation to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In time they learned Chinese speech, came to loathe the name Wa, and adopted the title Japan instead.

sentences.zh: 使者自言，國近日所出，以爲名。

translations.literal: The envoys themselves said that their state lay where the sun newly issues forth, and took this as its name.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys themselves explained that their realm lay where the sun first rises, and that they had taken this as their name.

sentences.zh: 或云日本乃小國，爲倭所并，故冒其號。

translations.literal: Some say Japan is a small state annexed by Wa, and therefore usurped that title.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that Japan was a petty domain swallowed up by Wa and had merely stolen the grander name.

sentences.zh: 使者不以情，故疑焉。

translations.literal: The envoys would not speak frankly—hence the doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Because the envoys would not speak plainly, skepticism remained.

sentences.zh: 又妄誇其國都方數千里，南、西盡海，東、北限大山，其外即毛人云。

translations.literal: They also boast falsely that their capital region measures thousands of li square; south and west reach the sea's limit, east and north are bounded by great mountains; beyond them are the hairy people, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: They also falsely claimed a capital domain thousands of li across—sea to the south and west, great mountains to the east and north—and said that beyond those mountains lived the hairy peoples.

sentences.zh: 長安元年，其王文武立，改元曰太寶，遣朝臣真人粟田貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chang'an, King Monmu ascended, changed the era name to Taihō, and sent the courtier Mahito Awata to present tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chang'an, King Monmu came to the throne, proclaimed the Taihō era, and sent the courtier Awata no Mahito to present local products.

sentences.zh: 朝臣真人者，猶唐尚書也。

translations.literal: Ason Mahito is like a Tang Shangshu.
translations.idiomatic: The title 'courtier Mahito' ranked much like a Tang minister of state.

sentences.zh: 冠進德冠，頂有華蘤四披，紫袍帛帶。

translations.literal: Crown: the Crown of Advancing Virtue; atop it four floral sprays draped; purple robe and silk belt.
translations.idiomatic: He wore the Crown of Advancing Virtue, its apex hung with four floral sprays, a purple robe, and a silken girdle.

sentences.zh: 真人好學，能屬文，進止有容。

translations.literal: Mahito loved learning, could compose prose, and in advancing and withdrawing had a composed bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Mahito was eager to learn, skilled at composition, and graceful in every movement.

sentences.zh: 武后宴之麟德殿，授司膳卿，還之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu feasted him in Linde Hall, appointed him Director of Palace Provisions, and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu entertained him in Linde Hall, made him Director of Palace Provisions, and let him return.

sentences.zh: 文武死，子阿用立。

translations.literal: Monmu died; his son Ahe ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Monmu died, and his son Ahe succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 死，子聖武立，改元曰白龜。

translations.literal: He died; his son Shōmu ascended and changed the era name to Hakki.
translations.idiomatic: Ahe died in turn; his son Shōmu took the throne and proclaimed the Hakki era.

sentences.zh: 開元初，粟田復朝，請從諸儒受經。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Awata came to court again and asked to study the classics with the literati.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Awata returned to court and asked leave to study the classics under the court scholars.

sentences.zh: 詔四門助教趙玄默即鴻臚寺爲師，獻大幅布爲贄，悉賞物貿書以歸。

translations.literal: An edict named Zhao Xuanmo, Assistant Instructor at the Four Gates, to serve as teacher at the Honglu Temple; he presented great bolts of cloth as gift; all rewards were given in goods exchanged for books to take home.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Zhao Xuanmo, assistant instructor at the Four Gates Academy, to instruct him at the Honglu Temple. Awata offered great bolts of cloth as tribute gifts; the court repaid him entirely in books and trade goods for the journey home.

sentences.zh: 其副朝臣仲滿慕華不肯去，易姓名曰朝衡，曆左補闕，儀王友，多所該識，久乃還。

translations.literal: His vice-envoy, Courtier Nakamaro, admired the splendor of China and refused to leave; he changed his surname and personal name to Chaoheng; passed through Left Reminder and Friend of the Prince of Yi; became deeply learned in many fields; only after long years did he return.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy, Nakamaro of the courtier clan, so loved Chinese civilization that he would not leave. He took the name Chaoheng, rose to Left Reminder and Friend of the Prince of Yi, and mastered many branches of learning before he went home at last—after many years.

sentences.zh: 聖武死，女孝明立，改元曰天平勝寶。

translations.literal: Shōmu died; his daughter Kōmyō ascended and changed the era name to Tenpyō-Shōhō.
translations.idiomatic: Shōmu died, and his daughter Kōmyō became sovereign, proclaiming the Tenpyō-Shōhō era.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載，朝衡復入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, Chaoheng came to court again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, Chaoheng presented himself at court once more.

sentences.zh: 上元中，擢左散騎常侍、安南都護。

translations.literal: During Shangyuan, he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant and Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan years he was raised to Left Regular Attendant and Protector-General of Annan.

sentences.zh: 新羅梗海道，更繇明、越州朝貢。

translations.literal: Silla obstructed the sea route; tribute came instead by way of Ming and Yue prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Silla blocked the sea lane, Japanese embassies were rerouted through Ming and Yue prefectures.

sentences.zh: 孝明死，大炊立。

translations.literal: Kōmyō died; Ōtomo ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Kōmyō died, and Ōtomo took the throne.

sentences.zh: 死，以聖武女高野姬爲王。

translations.literal: He died; Shōmu's daughter Takano no hime was made sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Ōtomo died in turn, and Shōmu's daughter Takano no hime was installed as ruler.

sentences.zh: 死，白壁立。

translations.literal: She died; Shirakabe ascended.
translations.idiomatic: She died as well, and Shirakabe succeeded her.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，使者真人興能獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, the envoy Mahito Ōneng presented tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong, the envoy Ōneng Mahito brought tribute to court.

sentences.zh: 真人，蓋因官而氏者也。

translations.literal: 'Mahito' was likely a surname taken from office.
translations.idiomatic: Mahito, it seems, was a family name derived from rank.

sentences.zh: 興能善書，其紙似繭而澤，人莫識。

translations.literal: Ōneng excelled at calligraphy; their paper was cocoon-like and lustrous—no one recognized it.
translations.idiomatic: Ōneng was a fine calligrapher; his paper felt like silk cocoons, glossy and strange—none at court had seen its like.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，其王曰桓武，遣使者朝。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan, the king was Kanmu, who sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan, King Kanmu sent ambassadors to court.

sentences.zh: 其學子橘免勢、浮屠空海願留肄業，曆二十餘年。

translations.literal: The students Kibi no Makibi and the monk Kūkai wished to remain to pursue studies, passing more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Students Kibi no Makibi and the monk Kūkai asked to stay on for study, and remained more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 使者高階真人來請免勢等俱還，詔可。

translations.literal: The envoy Takashina no Mahito came requesting that Makibi and the others all be sent back; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy Takashina no Mahito asked that Makibi and his fellows all be returned; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 次諾樂立，次嵯峨，次浮和，次仁明。

translations.literal: Next Noraku ascended, then Saga, then Fūwa, then Nimmei.
translations.idiomatic: Noraku followed, then Saga, then Fūwa, then Nimmei.

sentences.zh: 仁明直開成四年，復入貢。

translations.literal: Nimmei, reaching the fourth year of Kaicheng, again sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Nimmei, in the fourth year of Kaicheng, tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 次文德，次清和，次陽成。

translations.literal: Next Montoku, then Seiwa, then Yōzei.
translations.idiomatic: Montoku succeeded him, then Seiwa, then Yōzei.

sentences.zh: 次光孝，直光啟元年。

translations.literal: Next Kōkō, reaching the first year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Kōkō came next, reigning into the first year of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 其東海嶼中又有邪古、波邪、多尼三小王，北距新羅，西北百濟，西南直越州，有絲絮、怪珍云。

translations.literal: In the eastern sea isles were also three petty kings—Yegu, Boxie, and Duoni; north bordering Silla, northwest Baekje, southwest due toward Yue Prefecture—with silk floss and strange treasures, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern archipelago also held three lesser kings—Yegu, Boxie, and Duoni—lying north of Silla, northwest of Baekje, and due southwest of Yue Prefecture, where silk floss and curious treasures were found, or so it was said.

sentences.zh: 流鬼去京師萬五千里，直黑水靺鞨東北，少海之北，三面皆阻海，其北莫知所窮。

translations.literal: Liugui was fifteen thousand li from the capital, due northeast of Heishui Mohe, north of the Lesser Sea; on three sides all was sea-blocked; northward none knew the end.
translations.idiomatic: Liugui lay fifteen thousand li from the capital, northeast of the Heishui Mohe and north of the Lesser Sea. Sea hemmed it on three sides; to the north no one knew how far the land ran.

sentences.zh: 人依嶼散居，多沮澤，有魚鹽之利。

translations.literal: People dwelt scattered on islets; marshes were many; there was benefit in fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived on scattered islets amid widespread marshes, with fishing and salt to sustain them.

sentences.zh: 地蚤寒，多霜雪，以木廣六寸、長七尺系其上，以踐冰，逐走獸。

translations.literal: The land was ever cold, with much frost and snow; they tied planks six inches wide and seven feet long beneath the feet to tread ice and chase running beasts.
translations.idiomatic: The country was bitterly cold and snowbound. They lashed planks six inches wide and seven feet long to their feet to run over ice in pursuit of game.

sentences.zh: 土多狗，以皮爲裘。

translations.literal: Dogs were many in the land; skins served for fur coats.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs were plentiful; their pelts made winter clothing.

sentences.zh: 俗被發。

translations.literal: Custom: loose hair.
translations.idiomatic: The people wore their hair unbound.

sentences.zh: 粟似莠而小，無蔬蓏它穀。

translations.literal: Millet was like barnyard grass but small; no vegetables, melons, or other grains.
translations.idiomatic: Their grain was a millet small and coarse as barnyard grass; they grew no vegetables, melons, or other crops.

sentences.zh: 勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: Fighting men: ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They could field ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 南與莫曳靺鞨鄰，東南航海十五日行，乃至。

translations.literal: South they bordered Moyie Mohe; southeast by sea, fifteen days' sail brought one there.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay the Moyie Mohe; from the southeast one reached them by sea in fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，其王遣子可也余莫貂皮更三譯來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, the king sent his son Kayo with sable pelts; three interpreters relayed the message on his way to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan the king sent his son Kayo with sable furs, the tribute relayed through three rounds of interpretation before it reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 授騎都尉，遣之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Cavalry Commandant and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Cavalry Commandant and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，有儋羅者，其王儒李都羅遣使入朝，國居新羅武州南島上，俗樸陋，衣大豕皮，夏居革屋，冬窟室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo there was Danluo; King Yuli Duduo sent envoys to court; the state lay on an island south of Silla's Muzhou; customs were crude and plain; they wore great boar skins; in summer they dwelt in leather houses, in winter in pit-dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longshuo there appeared Danluo. King Yuli Duduo sent envoys to court. The kingdom stood on an island south of Silla's Muzhou; life there was rough and plain. Men wrapped themselves in boar hides, lived in leather shelters in summer and burrowed dwellings in winter.

sentences.zh: 地生五穀，耕不知用牛，以鐵齒杷土。

translations.literal: The land produced the five grains; in plowing they did not know to use cattle but used iron-toothed hoes on the soil.
translations.idiomatic: The five grains grew there, yet the people plowed without oxen, breaking the earth with iron-toothed mattocks.

sentences.zh: 初附百濟。

translations.literal: At first they submitted to Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: At first they owed allegiance to Baekje.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，酋長來朝，從帝至太山。

translations.literal: During Linde, a chieftain came to court and followed the emperor to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Linde era a chieftain came to court and accompanied the emperor to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 後附新羅。

translations.literal: Later they submitted to Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Later they fell under Silla's sway.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年，又有達末婁、達妒二部首領朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, there were also two tribal chiefs, Damolou and Dazu, who came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan two chieftains, Damolou and Dazu, likewise came bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 達末婁自言北扶餘之裔，高麗滅其國，遺人度那河，因居之，或曰他漏河，東北流入黑水。

translations.literal: Damolou said they were descendants of Northern Buyeo; when Goguryeo destroyed their state, survivors crossed the Na River and dwelt there—or the Talou River, which flows northeast into the Black Water.
translations.idiomatic: Damolou claimed descent from Northern Buyeo: when Goguryeo wiped out their kingdom, refugees forded the Na River and settled there—though some call it the Talou River, which runs northeast into the Black Water.

sentences.zh: 達姤，室韋種也，在那河陰，凍末河之東，西接黃頭室韋，東北距達末婁云。

translations.literal: Daji were a Shiwei tribe, on the south bank of the Na River, east of the Dongmo River; west they adjoined the Yellow-head Shiwei; northeast they bordered Damolou, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The Daji were a Shiwei people living south of the Na River and east of the Dongmo. Westward they met the Yellow-head Shiwei; to the northeast lay Damolou—or so the account runs.
